original:
lda sp+1
        inca
        ringup sp
        sta sp+1
proposal:
.if ::MODELB
        lda sp+1
        adc #0                      ; C = 1 (bcc :++ not taken): + 1
        cmp ringehi
        bcc :+
        rol sp                      ; sp is 0..7 here: C in 1, out 0
        sbc #>RINGBYTES             ; C = 0: A - $3A (the $80 fold's borrow); C = 1
        ror sp                      ; sp + $80: the low byte's fold; C = 1
:       sta sp+1
  .else
        inc sp+1                    ; at most $80: sp+1 < $80 (RINGEND = $8000)
        bpl :+
        lda #>RINGBASE              ; $80 folds to $30 = $80 - >RINGBYTES
        sta sp+1
:
  .endif
cycles: Per spnext expansion. No-carry path (bcc :++ taken) unchanged on both. Model B carry path: no fold 3+11(inca)+3+3(bcc)+3=23 -> 3+2+3+3+3=14; fold 43 -> 3+2+3+2+5+2+5+3=25. Master carry path: no fold lda3+inc a2+cmp2+bcc3+sta3=13 -> inc5+bpl3=8; fold 3+2+2+2+2+3=14 -> 5+2+2+3=12.
assumption: spnext is expanded 7x on Model B (TILCODE 4: engine.s 952,1129,2607,2657; SPR4CODE and SPR6CODE 1 each: 2372 via SPRITE_LOOPS; MNUCODE 1: menu.s 132) and 6x on Master (CODE 5, LOGIC 1). I measured this with ca65/ld65 map diffs. (1) On the carry path sp = old sp + 8 - 256 is in 0..7 whatever the caller (sp+8 <= $107), so the Model B low-byte fold (sp - $80 with borrow) is exactly sp+$80 and always borrows. (2) C = 1 at `lda sp+1` because bcc :++ fell through. (3) ringehi (zp, defs.inc:56) is $44 or $80 (select_backbuf), so A >= $44 on the fold path and A - $3A never borrows. (4) Master: sp+1 is a screen address high byte in $30..$7F (ring $3000-$7FFF, RINGEND = $8000, engine.s:153), so inc gives <= $80 and the fold input is exactly $80. (5) Exit state that changes: Model B fold path N=1 (was 0) and V may differ; mtmp is no longer written. Master carry path: A = sp low (no fold) or $30 (fold) instead of new sp+1; C = 1 (was 0 when no fold); N/V differ. Every caller is followed by dec/dex (N,Z rewritten) and A/C are dead: 952 -> dec tmp2 / bne @sc (ldy #7; lda (tp),y) or bra @runend (lda cnt; sec); 1129 -> dec tmp2 / bne @fsc (ldy/lda tp) or jmp @runend; 2372 -> dec sp_cnt / ds_colloop -> jmp sprFN (SPRFULL/SPRMSK entries start lda tmp2; no adc/sbc/rol/ror before a cmp in SPRLINE/MPAIR) or ds_rowdone (lda sp_row); 2607 -> dex / beq @done (rts from copy_partial -> engine.s:3125 jsr blank_below: lda wfine) else lda ptr; clc; 2657 -> dex / bne @char (lda #0) or rts from blank_below -> stza NSPR (Master stz, A/flags kept) -> t_build_sections (pha/pla, then build_sections: lda curbuf; asl), or PARALLAX pl_draw (ldx/lda); menu.s:132 -> dec tmp4 / bne @pair (lda #0) or lda tp. No bvc/bvs anywhere near (only engine.s:3700 in the ISR after its own bit).
anon_change: none: each target still emits exactly two ':' per spnext (Model B: the fold skip and the final one, replacing ringup's and the final; Master: the bpl target and the final), so bcc :++ and every caller's counting across spnext are unchanged; the ca65 warning list is identical (the same 5 unreferenced-label warnings, shifted)
argument: Model B: adc #0 with C=1 == inca (+1; A <= $80 so no carry out); cmp ringehi/bcc as in ringup. Fold: rol sp (C in 1) -> sp'=2sp+1 <= 15, C out 0 (bit 7 of sp is 0); sbc #$39 with C=0 -> A-$3A == original (A-$39) then sbc #0 with the borrow of sp-$80 (always, sp<$80); C out 1; ror sp with C=1 -> $80|(2sp+1)>>1 = sp+$80 == original sp-$80 mod 256, C out = bit 0 of 2sp+1 = 1 == original C=1 after sbc #0; sta sp+1 identical. A at exit identical on all paths. Master: inc sp+1 then bpl == lda/inc a/cmp #$80/bcc since sp+1+1 <= $80 and >= $80 means exactly $80; fold stores $30 == $80 - $50. sp+1 value identical on all paths. Checked in a scratch copy with all 4 candidates applied: both targets built (full build.sh + modelb/build.sh). tools/gate.sh at 200 and 800 frames: every Master check and Model B lockstep L0/L5 and pix L0/L6 identical. B title's time-sampled RAM compare differs only during boot staging (code bytes in main RAM) and matches from 16M cycles on; any 1-byte change in a bank does the same. B lockstep L12 at 800 frames times out identically on the unmodified source.
review: Original lines 526-529 match. The carry path always has sp in 0..7 (lda sp/clc/adc #8), and C=1 at lda sp+1. Model B: adc #0 = inca, and cmp/bcc are unchanged. On the fold path, rol sp (C in 1, out 0) / sbc #$39 (C=0, so A-$3A with no borrow because A>=$44) / ror sp (C in 1) gives sp+$80 and A-$3A with C=1, the same as the original. Only N (now 1) and V (1 when A=$80) change on the fold path. Master: inc sp+1 <= $80, so bpl gives the same fold test and $30 is the fold of $80. A and C change on the carry path. I traced every consumer on both targets and nothing reads them. 952 (dec tmp2 -> ldy/lda, or lda cnt;sec), 1129 (Master @fsc lda tp; @runend sec), 2372 (dec sp_cnt -> jmp sprFN, whose entries are lda tmp2;cmp #7; ds_rowdone lda), 2607 (dex -> rts -> blank_below lda wfine, whose @no path goes to stz NSPR -> t_build_sections pha/pla -> lda curbuf;asl; else lda ptr;clc), 2657 (dex -> lda #0, or rts as above), menu.s:132 (dec tmp4 -> lda #0/asl, or lda tp). Every bvc/bvs (logic.s macros, display.s:141, engine 3700) sets V itself first. The ISR does not touch sp. Each target still emits 2 ':' per spnext, and ca65's warnings are identical. Measured by assembling both targets: Master CODE 15 + LOGIC 3 = 18; Model B TILCODE 44, SPR4CODE 11, SPR6CODE 11, MNUCODE 11 = 77. Cycles checked: Model B 23->14 / 43->25, Master 13->8 / 14->12.

original:
lda p                       ; borrows from A when p is below $80
        sec
        sbc #<RINGBYTES
proposal:
lda p                       ; borrows from A when p is below $80 (C = 1 still)
        sbc #<RINGBYTES
cycles: Model B ringup fold path -2 (sec gone), non-fold unchanged; Master unchanged (MODELB branch only). 14 bytes = 7 direct ringup sites + the 7 inside spnext; if the spnext candidate (i0110) is applied first, 7 (TILCODE 3, LGCCODE 1, SPR4CODE 1, SPR6CODE 1, MNUCODE 1).
assumption: None outside the macro: the fall-through of `bcc :+` after `cmp ringehi` has C=1; `sbc #>RINGBYTES` ($39) from A >= ringehi >= $44 does not borrow so C stays 1 (the macro's own comment says so); pha and lda p do not touch C.
argument: sec only ever runs with C already 1, so it does nothing; everything else is identical.
review: Lines 499-501 match. On the fold path, cmp ringehi leaves C=1. sbc #$39 from A >= ringehi >= $44 cannot borrow, and pha and lda p leave C alone, so sec is a no-op. The fold path is 2 cycles faster. The Model B saving, measured, is 7 bytes applied after index 0 (TILCODE 3, LGCCODE 1, SPR4 1, SPR6 1, MNUCODE 1). Applied on its own it is 14, because the spnext copies are included.

original:
cmp #>RINGEND
        bcc :+
        sbc #>RINGBYTES
proposal:
bpl :+                      ; RINGEND = $8000: N from A (every caller's adc / inc a)
        sec
        sbc #>RINGBYTES
cycles: Master only: no fold cmp2+bcc3=5 -> bpl3; fold cmp2+bcc2+sbc2=6 -> bpl2+sec2+sbc2=6. 11 bytes if applied alone (5 direct sites: engine.s 554, 963, 2405, 2617, menu.s 106; + 6 spnext expansions); 5 (CODE 4, LOGIC 1) if the spnext candidate (i0110) is applied first. Both figures measured.
assumption: (1) RINGEND = RINGBASE + RINGBYTES = $3000 + $5000 = $8000 on the Master (engine.s:140-153; RINGROWS=32 fixed), so A >= >RINGEND <=> bit 7 of A. (2) N reflects A at every Master expansion: 554 `adc RINGHI,x`; 963 `adc #>ROWBYTES`; 2405 `adc #>ROWBYTES`; 2617 `inca` (= inc a); 3310 (PARALLAX) `adc #0`; menu.s:106 `adc #>ROWBYTES`; spnext `inc a`; 4841 is inside the MODELB branch (engine.s:4801 .else of 4742 .if .not MODELB). (3) Exit flags change only on the no-fold path: N=0 (was 1), C = entry C (was 0). Entry C is 0 at every adc site (sum < $100) and 1 at 2617 and in spnext. Consumers: every site stores A and then goes to: 554 rts -> ringaddr callers 628 (sta/lda), 1878 (lda sp), 2513 (lda sp; clc), 2650 (ldx), 3324 (lda sp), menu m_ringaddr (ldx #0); 963 rts -> inc rc_y; 2405 jmp ds_rowloop (lda); 2617 bra @fjmp -> jmp @g4 (ldy/lda/sta/dey only, then spnext's clc); 3310 jsr @tile (lda pl_cx+1, C=0 as before since entry C=0); menu.s:106 -> lda GLYPHBUF,x; spnext -> dec/dex (see i0110). Fold path flags identical (sec+sbc == cmp-set C=1 + sbc).
anon_change: none: the ':' after the sbc is kept
argument: bpl :+ skips iff A < $80 == cmp #$80/bcc; on the fold path sec supplies the C=1 the cmp used to, so sbc #$50 gives the same A and flags.
review: Lines 507-509 match. The Master's RINGEND is $8000, so for an 8-bit A, A>=$80 exactly when bit 7 is set. At every Master site N reflects A: 554 adc RINGHI,x, 963/2405/menu:106 adc #>ROWBYTES, 2617 inc a, 3310 adc #0 (PARALLAX), spnext inc a if index 0 is not applied. 4841 is Model B only. On the fold path, sec+sbc matches the flags and A of cmp(C=1)+sbc. On the no-fold path, C is now the entry C instead of 0, N=0 instead of 1, and Z is unchanged (A>=$30). The entry C is 0 at every adc site, so only 2617 (C=1) differs. That path goes bra @fjmp -> @g4/@g2/@g0 (ldy/lda/sta), then spnext's clc, so nothing reads the carry. The N consumers are all reloads: ringaddr callers use A, rts->inc rc_y, jmp ds_rowloop lda, @tile lda/lsr, lda GLYPHBUF. Measured: 5 bytes on the Master after index 0 (CODE 4, LOGIC 1), 11 on its own. Model B unchanged. Cycles: 5->3 with no fold, 6->6 on the fold.

original:
rol sp+1                    ; sp+1:A = cx*8
        clc
        adc RINGLO,x
proposal:
rol sp+1                    ; sp+1:A = cx*8; C = 0 (cx < 8192)
        adc RINGLO,x
cycles: -2 on both (ringaddr, every call); Model B TILCODE -1, Master CODE -1 (measured)
assumption: C after the third `rol sp+1` is bit 13 of cx (w16). Every caller passes a map char column: rc_x (drawrect, engine.s:602-604), wcx+sp_c0 (1755-1766), wcx+tmp4 (2488-2496), wcx (2645), pl_cx (PARALLAX). Maps are <= 256 tiles = 1024 chars wide (engine.s:610 comment), so w16+1 <= 4. Stronger still: if bit 13 of cx were set, cx*8 would already be cut to 16 bits and the original's single-fold ring address would be wrong. So every correct run of the original has C=0 here.
argument: clc only ever runs with C already 0, so it does nothing; adc RINGLO,x and everything after it are identical.
review: Lines 548-550 match. After the third rol, C is bit 13 of w16. Every caller passes a non-negative map column below 1024. drawrect's rc_x comes from wcx, is clipped to >= wcx by drawrect_clip, or is wcx+... with no borrow. sp_c0 and tmp4 are added to wcx with a zero high byte (adc #0). wcx is used directly, pl_cx=wcx, and the menu sets w16+1=0. So C=0 and clc is redundant, saving 2 cycles. Measured: Master CODE -1, Model B TILCODE -1. ringaddr7 (engine.s:4819) is a separate copy and is untouched.

original: inca
proposal:
.if ::MODELB
        adc #0                      ; C = 1 (the bcc fell through): +1, 2 bytes not 6
  .else
        inca
  .endif
cycles: Model B: page-crossing path 11 -> 2 (inca = sta/inc/lda mtmp); bcc-taken path unchanged. Master: identical code.
assumption: Inside spnext only: the path reaching this line is the fall-through of `bcc :++` after `adc #8`, so C = 1; `lda sp+1` leaves C alone. D is clear (the game uses binary adc everywhere). The flags/C out of the increment are dead: ringup's first instruction (cmp ringehi) overwrites N,Z,C. mtmp is scratch owned by the expansions (nothing reads it after). 4 bytes per expansion x 7 Model B expansions: engine.s 952, 1129, 2372 (SPRITE_LOOPS, expanded in spr4 SPR4CODE and spr6 SPR6CODE), 2607, 2657, menu.s 132. The change is outside the unrolled computed-entry sprite line code (sprnext is the column advance).
argument: inca (6502: sta mtmp / inc mtmp / lda mtmp) gives A = sp+1 + 1 with C preserved (=1). adc #0 with C = 1 gives A = sp+1 + 1 (C out differs only when sp+1 = $FF, and is immediately overwritten by ringup's cmp). Same A into ringup, same ringup outcome, same sta sp+1. The bcc :++ target count is unchanged (no labels added). Uses ::MODELB since spnext is expanded inside .scope spr4/spr6.
review: Line 527 is the inca in spnext. The only way to it is the fall-through of bcc :++ after clc/adc #8, so C = 1, and lda sp+1 leaves C alone. No code in the tree uses sed, so D is clear. adc #0 gives A = sp+1 + 1, the same as inca. N, Z and C are overwritten by ringup's cmp before anything reads them. V is 0 on both versions: adc #8 cannot overflow with sp >= $F8, and adc #0 cannot overflow with sp+1 <= $7E on the no-fold path; on the fold path ringup's sbc sets V either way. No labels are added. Built: the Master CLEO is byte-identical; on the Model B TILCODE is 16 bytes smaller (4 expansions), SPR4CODE 4, SPR6CODE 4 and MNUCODE 4, 28 in all, and every link assert passes.

original:
rol sp+1                    ; sp+1:A = cx*8
        clc
        adc RINGLO,x
proposal:
rol sp+1                    ; sp+1:A = cx*8 (C = 0: cx < 8192)
        adc RINGLO,x
cycles: single path 2 cycles faster on both targets
assumption: After the third `rol sp+1`, C = bit 5 of w16+1, which is 0 because every caller's w16 is a map char column < 1024 (maps are 32..256 tiles wide, low.s:86): drawrect (rc_x, window clipped by drawrect_clip / scroll_validate), copy_partial engine.s:2493-2498 (wcx + col), blank_below 2644-2648 (wcx), pl walker 3324 (pl_cx = w16, walked from wcx), menu.s:91-96 (tx>>1, w16+1 = 0), Master sprite path 1878 (wcx + sp_c0), the TOMAIN far thunk (same callers). ringaddr7 (bank 7 copy) is separate and not changed.
argument: asl (C=bit7 of w16) / rol sp+1 (C out = bit7 of w16+1) / asl / rol (C=bit6 of w16+1) / asl / rol (C = bit5 of w16+1 = 0). So clc is a no-op; adc RINGLO,x adds with C = 0 as before.
review: After the three asl/rol pairs, C = bit 5 of w16+1, which is 0 whenever cx < 8192. I checked every caller. drawrect gets rc_x = wcx + 0..79 through drawrect_clip or scroll_validate. copy_partial passes wcx + col, blank_below passes wcx, and the pl walker passes wcx plus at most VISLINES/4. The Master sprite path passes wcx + sp_c0 with sp_c0 in 0..79. The menu passes tx>>1 with a zero high byte. Every map is under 1024 chars wide. The adc sees the same C = 0, so clc is a no-op. Built: CODE and TILCODE are each 1 byte smaller.

original:
lda rc_x                    ; dirty column range (rects are window-clipped, so
        sec                         ; the low byte of rc_x - wcx is the column)
        sbc wcx
proposal:
lda rc_x                    ; dirty column range (rects are window-clipped, so
        sbc wcx                     ; the low byte of rc_x - wcx is the column; C = 1 from cmp wcy)
cycles: this path 2 cycles faster on both; other paths untouched
assumption: None outside the window: the only way here is the fall-through of `cmp wcy / bne :+` (line 587-588), i.e. rc_y = wcy, so C = 1; `ldx curbuf` and `lda rc_x` do not touch C. No label on the sec line.
argument: cmp with equal operands sets C = 1; bne not taken means equal. sec is therefore redundant; sbc wcx computes the same value and flags.
review: The only way to line 590 is the fall-through of cmp wcy / bne :+, where rc_y == wcy, so C = 1. ldx curbuf and lda rc_x leave C alone, and the sec line has no label. Built: 1 byte smaller on both targets.

proposal:
@plo:   clc
        adc rc_w
  .if MODELB
        sbc #0                      ; C = 0 (col + rc_w <= 80): the -1
  .else
        deca
  .endif
cycles: Model B: 11 -> 2 (deca = sta/dec/lda mtmp); Master identical code
assumption: col + rc_w < 256 so adc leaves C = 0: col = rc_x - wcx is 0..79 and col + rc_w <= 80 for every drawrect entry (drawrect_clip engine.s:3366-3432 clips to ROWCHARS; scroll_validate 1180-1232 builds col 0 or 80-dx with rc_w = dx, or col 0 w 80). Only C/N/Z differ afterwards and `cmp PART_HI,x` (line 599) overwrites them all.
argument: deca on the 6502 = A-1 with C preserved; sbc #0 with C = 0 = A - 0 - 1 = A-1 (mod 256, including A = 0 -> $FF when rc_w = 0 and col = 0). Same A into cmp PART_HI,x / sta PART_HI,x.
review: col = rc_x - wcx is 0..79 and col + rc_w <= 80 on every path in: drawrect_clip's @right and rel<0 clips, and scroll_validate's dx-/dx+/@dorows/@full rects. So adc rc_w leaves C = 0, and sbc #0 gives A - 1, which matches deca, including 0 -> $FF. cmp PART_HI,x overwrites N, Z and C. This is Model B only: the Master CLEO is byte-identical, and TILCODE is 4 bytes smaller.

original:
lda rc_x+1
        sta w16+1                   ; the ring address's copy, from this load too
        lsr
        sta tmp
        lda rc_x
        ror
        lsr tmp
        ror                         ; A = tx0 (map width <= 256 tiles)
proposal:
lda rc_x+1
        sta w16+1                   ; the ring address's copy, from this load too
        lsr                         ; C = bit 0, A = bit 1 (rc_x+1 <= 3)
        tax
        lda rc_x
        ror
        cpx #1                      ; C = bit 1
        ror                         ; A = tx0 (map width <= 256 tiles)
cycles: single path: sta tmp 3 -> tax 2, lsr tmp 5 -> cpx #1 2: 4 cycles faster on both
assumption: rc_x+1 <= 3 (rc_x < 1024: maps are at most 256 tiles = 1024 chars wide, low.s:86, and the existing comment already assumes tx0 fits a byte), so X = rc_x+1 >> 1 is 0 or 1 and cpx #1 sets C = that bit. X is dead: nothing reads X between here and ringaddr, whose ringmod/tax overwrites it first (Master RINGROWS=32: and #31 then tax; Model B: ringmod's n2: tax). tmp is dead: its next uses in drawrect (@ghalf, @hcopy, @tpset, @hfill, @fillgo) and in maprow5/maprow/mapstrip all write it before reading.
argument: Original: C = hi bit0 into first ror, then lsr tmp puts hi bit1 into C for the second ror; tmp ends = hi>>2 (unused). New: lsr leaves A = hi>>1 in {0,1}, kept in X; cpx #1 gives C = (X >= 1) = hi bit1 without touching A. Same A = tx0; the C out of the final ror is bit1 of rc_x in both.
review: rc_x < 1024 (it is window-clipped, and every map is at most 1024 chars wide), so rc_x+1 <= 3. After lsr, X is 0 or 1, and cpx #1 sets C to bit 1 of the high byte, as lsr tmp did. A and the final C are identical. X is dead: nothing in 611-627 reads it, and ringaddr's ringmod/tax writes it first on both targets. tmp is dead: every drawrect that gets this far writes tmp in @tpset or @solid/@fillgo (Master and Model B) before it reads it, so what the callers see on return is unchanged. Built: 1 byte smaller on both.

original:
lda rc_x                    ; tiles-1 = tx1 - tx0 = ((rc_x & 3) + rc_w - 1) >> 2,
        sta w16                     ; the copy the ring address needs, from the same load
        and #3                      ; so tx1 never needs building: max 3 + 80 - 1 = 82,
        sta rc_sc0
        clc                         ; one byte, no 16-bit shift, no w16
        adc rc_w
        deca
        lsr
        lsr
        sta rc_nt
        lda rc_sc0
        asl
        asl
        asl
        sta rc_ro0
proposal:
lda rc_x                    ; tiles-1 = tx1 - tx0 = ((rc_x & 3) + rc_w - 1) >> 2,
        sta w16                     ; the copy the ring address needs, from the same load
        and #3                      ; so tx1 never needs building: max 3 + 80 - 1 = 82,
        sta rc_sc0                  ; one byte, no 16-bit shift, no w16
        asl
        asl
        asl                         ; C = 0 (rc_sc0 < 4): the adc's clc
        sta rc_ro0
        lda rc_sc0
        adc rc_w
  .if MODELB
        sbc #0                      ; C = 0 (<= 83, no carry): the -1
  .else
        deca
  .endif
        lsr
        lsr
        sta rc_nt
cycles: single path: Master 2 faster (clc gone); Model B 11 faster (clc gone, deca 11 -> sbc #0 2)
assumption: rc_w <= 80 (drawrect_clip / scroll_validate), so (rc_x & 3) + rc_w <= 83 and the adc leaves C = 0 for the Model B sbc #0. Nothing between here and ringaddr reads rc_nt or rc_ro0, so storing ro0 before nt is invisible; the C/N/Z left at the end are dead (lda rc_y then ringaddr: ringmod's cmp (Model B) / the asl's (Master) set C before any use).
argument: Reordered: ro0 = sc0<<3 first; three asl of a value < 4 shift out zeros, so C = 0 exactly where the old clc stood (sta/lda do not touch C). lda rc_sc0 restores A = sc0; adc rc_w with C = 0 = sc0 + w; Master dec a / Model B sbc #0 (C = 0, no carry out of the adc) = sc0 + w - 1; lsr lsr; sta rc_nt. Same stored values in rc_sc0, rc_ro0, rc_nt, w16.
review: ro0 = sc0<<3 is stored first. Three asl of a value under 4 shift out zeros, so C = 0 where the clc was. lda rc_sc0 / adc rc_w: the sum is at most 83, so C = 0 after it. On the Model B, sbc #0 is therefore -1, the same as deca. rc_nt, rc_ro0, rc_sc0 and w16 get the same stores. The A left at the end differs but is dead (lda rc_y is next), and ringaddr sets C before using it (Master asl, Model B ringmod cmp). rc_w = 0 gives the same result as well. Built: CODE is 1 byte smaller and TILCODE 5.

original:
@rowy:
  .if MODELB
        jsr mapstrip                ; the row's rc_nt+1 map bytes into MAPBUF, likewise
        wrsel BANK_TILES, BANK_TILES ; (mapstrip comes back with A = this bank: the
  .endif                            ;  write bank too, done here rather than in low RAM)
proposal:
THREE HUNKS (one change):
--- HUNK 1: src/engine.s lines 653-657 become:
@rowy:
  .if MODELB
        wrsel BANK_TILES, BANK_TILES ; (mapstrip comes back with A = this bank: the
  .endif                            ;  write bank too, done here rather than in low RAM)
--- HUNK 2: src/engine.s lines 777-780, original:
  .if .not MODELB
        setbank BANK_MAP            ; @drawrow left the tile bank selected
  .endif
        jmp @rowy
--- become:
  .if .not MODELB
        setbank BANK_MAP            ; @drawrow left the tile bank selected
  .else
        jsr mapstrip                ; the next row's map bytes (maprow5 fetched the first)
  .endif
        jmp @rowy
--- HUNK 3: modelb/src/low.s line 98 (`        rts`, maprow5's last line, directly before mapstrip:) is deleted, so maprow5 falls into mapstrip; update maprow5's comment (line 89) to say it also fetches the first strip.
cycles: Model B first tile row: 12 faster (one jsr/rts pair gone); every later row: jmp @rowy + jsr mapstrip -> jsr mapstrip + jmp @rowy, identical. Master unchanged.
assumption: maprow5's only caller is engine.s:639 (grep: no other reference); mapstrip immediately follows maprow5 in the same segment LOWCODE (low.s:98-100). mapstrip's other caller dirfetch (low.s:120) is unaffected. mapstrip only needs ptr and rc_nt, both set before maprow5 is called (rc_nt at 621, ptr by maprow5 itself); it does not inspect the stack. The saved byte is in LOWCODE (low RAM, full). wrsel's recorded site is neither moved relative to its label nor resized; A at @rowy is the bank from mapstrip on both entry paths (jmp does not touch A).
argument: Before: maprow5 ... rts; @rowy: jsr mapstrip; wrsel. After: maprow5 ... falls into mapstrip ... rts back to drawrect directly before @rowy: wrsel -- same sequence of effects for the first row. For later rows @nextrow now calls mapstrip itself before jmp @rowy, so @rowy still runs wrsel with the fresh strip in MAPBUF. bank 5 bytes net 0 (jsr moved), low RAM -1.
review: I applied all three hunks and built. The Master CLEO is byte-identical. On the Model B, LOWCODE is 1 byte smaller and TILCODE is the same size. maprow5's only caller is engine.s:639, and mapstrip directly follows it in LOWCODE. For the first row, drawrect runs no bank-5 code between the two calls (the jsr maprow5 is the last instruction before @rowy), so the order of effects is the same. Later rows run jsr mapstrip before jmp @rowy. @rowy's only reference is the jmp at 780. dirfetch is unaffected. The BANKREF/WRREC records are recomputed by the assembler, and neither wrsel nor bankimm changes size. LOWCODE has no fixed offsets (only the size < 256 assert), and ldprog/loader take addresses from labels.txt on every pass.

Every path stores the same rc_* values: @full (from 1155 jmp, 1175/1178/1191/1211/1219) now does lda #BUFROWS/sta rc_h/lda wcy/sta rc_y and falls into @dorows; dy<0 has A=-dy in 1..30, so Z=0 after inc a (Master) or after inca's lda mtmp (Model B), and the bne is always taken; dy>0 gains bra @dorows and loses the bra @done. jsr drawrect falls into @done (line 1240), which reads no flags before ldx/asl. drawrect's flags on entry are the same as before (lda #ROWCHARS/sta). No ':' labels added or removed; @seth is unique in scope. Cycles: dy<0 -3, @full -6, dy>0 and dy=0 unchanged, on both targets. Assembled: Master CODE -8, Model B TILCODE -10.

original:
cmp #<-30
        bcc @full
        eor #$FF
        inca
proposal:
cmp #<-30
        bcc @full
        eor #$FF
  .if MODELB
        adc #0                      ; C = 1 from the cmp: A = -A (inca is 6 bytes here)
  .else
        inca
  .endif
cycles: Model B: the inca expansion (sta mtmp 3, inc mtmp 5, lda mtmp 3 = 11) becomes adc #0 (2), 9 cycles faster. Master unchanged.
assumption: C = 1 at the eor, because the bcc @full just above was not taken. A = w16b is $E2..$FF, so ~A is 0..$1D and there is no carry out. C leaves as 0 instead of 1, and nothing reads C before drawrect's own sec/cmp. The path is sta rc_h, lda wcy, sta rc_y, the rc_x loads and stores, lda #ROWCHARS, sta rc_w, jsr drawrect; drawrect (engine.s:563) starts lda rc_h / bne, then on the Model B lda mrow / sec. Z after the adc = (A = 0) = 0, the same as after inca's lda mtmp, so the bne @seth of the layout candidate (or the original bra) is unaffected. mtmp is no longer written; it is scratch owned by the macro expansions and nothing reads it across this point.
argument: eor #$FF then +1 is a two's-complement negate; with C = 1 known, adc #0 adds exactly 1. This applies whether or not the layout candidate (window i0653) is taken, since that candidate keeps these lines verbatim.
review: C=1 after the bcc @full is not taken; A=$E2..$FF, so eor gives 0..$1D and adc #0 gives 1..$1E with C=0, Z=0, N=0, V=0. Nothing reads C or V before drawrect, which begins lda rc_h/bne, then (Model B) lda mrow/sec/sbc. Z=0 keeps i0653's bne @seth taken. Model B: 11 cycles become 2. Assembled: TILCODE -4 (-15 with i0653 and i0657).

original:
lda #1
        sta BUF_VALID,x
        stz BUF_BOTOK,x             ; the window moved: the slot below is stale again
proposal:
lda #1
        sta BUF_VALID,x
  .if MODELB
        lsr                         ; A = 0: a byte shorter than stz's lda #0
        sta BUF_BOTOK,x             ; the window moved: the slot below is stale again
  .else
        stz BUF_BOTOK,x             ; the window moved: the slot below is stale again
  .endif
cycles: Model B: lda #0 (2 cycles) becomes lsr (2 cycles), so no change. Master unchanged.
assumption: A = 1 from the lda #1 two lines up. Nothing reads C before the asl at line 1248 overwrites it (only lda wcy / sta BUF_CY,x / txa in between), so the C = 1 left by lsr is dead.
argument: lsr of 1 gives 0 with N = 0 and Z = 1, exactly as lda #0 does; the sta BUF_BOTOK,x is then the same as the stz expansion.
review: A=1 from lda #1, so lsr gives A=0, Z=1, N=0 (as lda #0 does) and C=1. C is dead: it is overwritten by the asl at 1248 before any read (lda wcy/sta/txa come between). 2 cycles become 2. Assembled: Model B TILCODE -1.

original: stza tmp4                   ; i
proposal: stz tmp4                    ; i
cycles: Model B: pha / lda #0 / sta / pla (12 cycles) becomes lda #0 / sta (5), 7 faster. Master identical (stz zp).
assumption: A is dead: the next instruction (line 1269) is lda recp, which also overwrites N and Z.
argument: stza differs from stz only in preserving A, and A is reloaded straight away.
review: lda recp comes next and overwrites A, N and Z. On the Master both spellings are stz zp; on the Model B the pha/pla pair goes. Assembled: LGCCODE -2.

original: stza KEEP,x
proposal: stz KEEP,x
cycles: Model B: 14 cycles become 7. Master identical (stz abs,x).
assumption: A is dead afterwards: both successors reload A before reading it, the fall-through with lda sprmul5,x (1279) and bcs @next with lda rp (1315). The cpx cnt at 1277 rewrites N, Z and C straight away.
argument: stza differs from stz only in preserving A (pha/pla) and in the N and Z left by the pla; neither is observed.
review: The cpx cnt that follows rewrites N, Z and C. Both successors reload A (lda sprmul5,x at 1279; lda rp at @next 1315) and nothing else branches in between. Master is identical; Model B loses pha/pla, 14 cycles become 7. Assembled: LGCCODE -2.

original: ldaz rp
proposal:
.if MODELB
        lda (rp),y                  ; Y = 0 from the cmpz above
  .else
        ldaz rp
  .endif
cycles: Model B: ldy #0 + lda (rp),y (7 cycles) becomes lda (rp),y (5). Master unchanged.
assumption: On the Model B, the cmpz rp at line 1282 expands to ldy #0 / cmp (rp),y. Between it and line 1289 there are only beq, cmp # and bcc, none of which touch Y. Y's final value (0) is unchanged.
argument: The same load, with Y already 0.
review: Model B cmpz rp at 1282 is ldy #0/cmp (rp),y. Only beq/cmp #/bcc lie between it and 1289, there are no labels or branch-ins, and Y stays 0. Master unchanged. Assembled: LGCCODE -2.

original: bra @pos
proposal: bne @pos
cycles: bra (Master 3 cycles; Model B jmp, 3 cycles) becomes a taken bne, 3 cycles on both.
assumption: A = 1 from the lda #1 on the line before, so Z = 0 and the bne is always taken.
argument: An unconditional branch replaced by a branch on a flag whose value is known.
review: The lda #1 just before sets Z=0, so the bne is always taken: 3 cycles, as bra/jmp. Assembled: Model B LGCCODE -1; Master unchanged.

original: ldy #1
proposal:
.if MODELB
        iny                         ; Y = 0 on both ways in (cmpz, ldaz)
  .else
        ldy #1
  .endif
cycles: Model B: ldy #1 (2 cycles) becomes iny (2 cycles). Master unchanged.
assumption: On the Model B, @same is reached only by the beq at 1283, straight after cmpz's ldy #0, so Y = 0. The other way in comes through ldaz rp at 1289 (ldy #0 / lda (rp),y, or, with the i0692 candidate, lda (rp),y with Y still 0 from the cmpz). Nothing in between touches Y: lda #1, lda #2 and sta tmp3 leave it alone. The lda SPRLIST+1,x that follows overwrites the N and Z set by iny.
argument: With Y = 0, iny gives Y = 1, the same as ldy #1.
review: There are two ways into @pos: fall-through from 1293 (after ldaz's ldy #0, or cmpz's with i0692) and @same, reached only from the beq at 1283 after cmpz's ldy #0. Y=0 on both on the Model B, and lda #1/#2 and sta tmp3 leave Y alone. The iny flags are overwritten by lda SPRLIST+1,x. Assembled: LGCCODE -1.

original:
:       inc tmp4
        bra @l
proposal:
:       inc tmp4
        bne @l                      ; always: i+1 <= MAXSPR
cycles: bra (3 cycles; jmp 3 on the Model B) becomes a taken bne, 3 cycles on both.
assumption: tmp4 = i < NSPR <= MAXSPR (24 on the Model B build, 32 on the Master; addsprite at engine.s:1382 caps NSPR at MAXSPR), so inc tmp4 gives 1..MAXSPR and never 0.
argument: inc sets Z from its result, which is nonzero. The anonymous ':' on the inc line is kept.
review: Every path to the ':' at 1321 passes the cpx NSPR/bcs @done check with tmp4=i<NSPR<=255, and the loop never writes tmp4 elsewhere. So i+1 is 1..255 and Z=0: the bne is always taken, 3 cycles. The ':' is kept, so the count is unchanged. Assembled: LGCCODE -1.

original: @pass:  stza spi
proposal: @pass:  stz spi                     ; A dead: lda recp next
cycles: Master identical (stz zp, 3). Model B: stza=pha/lda#0/sta zp/pla 12 cy -> lda#0/sta zp 5 cy.
assumption: A dead at @pass: the next instruction (engine.s:1407) is lda recp; both entries (fall-through from sta dpass at 1405, jmp @pass at 1464) carry no live A. N,Z from stz's 6502 expansion are overwritten by lda recp.
argument: stza keeps A through pha/pla; A is overwritten by the very next lda recp, so the A-preserving spelling is unneeded; stz (lda #0/sta spi on 6502, stz spi on 65C02) stores the same zero. Flags: lda recp sets N,Z anew; C/V untouched by both forms.
review: A is dead at @pass. The next instruction is lda recp on both entries (the fall-through and the jmp/bpl from @endpass). stz spi stores the same 0, lda recp sets N,Z again, and C/V are untouched. Master output is byte-identical; a scratch assemble shows Model B LGCCODE 2 bytes smaller.

original:
@l:     ldx spi
        cpx NSPR
        bcs @endpass
        lda sprmul5,x
        tax
        lda SPRLIST,x
        cmp #BOXID0
        lda dpass
        adc #$FF
        beq @next
        lda SPRLIST,x
        cmp #BOXID0+BOXN            ; a box star the logic says nothing can disturb, and
        bcc @write                  ; the same frame already in the same place: if
        ldy spi                     ; nothing has been repainted under it, its pixels
        lda KEEP,y                  ; are still right, so leave it alone
proposal:
@l:     ldy spi
        cpy NSPR
        bcs @endpass
        ldx sprmul5,y
        ldy SPRLIST,x               ; Y = id for both compares
        cpy #BOXID0
        lda dpass
        adc #$FF
        beq @next
        cpy #BOXID0+BOXN            ; a box star the logic says nothing can disturb, and
        bcc @write                  ; the same frame already in the same place: if
        ldy spi                     ; nothing has been repainted under it, its pixels
        lda KEEP,y                  ; are still right, so leave it alone
cycles: loop head: ldx spi/cpx/lda sprmul5,x/tax (3+c+4+2) -> ldy spi/cpy/ldx sprmul5,y (3+c+4): -2 cy; lda SPRLIST,x/cmp -> ldy SPRLIST,x/cpy: same (4+2); second lda SPRLIST,x (4 cy) removed: -4 cy on every path that reaches it. bcs @endpass path: same. Both targets identical counts (no macros).
assumption: X and Y are not live into @l from either entry (jmp/bne @l at 1460, fall-through from 1410): X is recomputed from sprmul5 and Y reloaded before every use (@write does ldy #1 at 1431, the KEEP path does ldy spi, kept). cpy abs/zp, ldx abs,y, ldy abs,x, cpy #imm all exist on the NMOS 6502. The @endpass path (1462-1468) reloads X (ldx curbuf) and uses no Y.
argument: ldy spi/cpy NSPR sets C exactly as ldx spi/cpx NSPR. ldx sprmul5,y loads the same byte that lda sprmul5,x + tax put in X (index spi in both). ldy SPRLIST,x/cpy #BOXID0 gives the same C as lda SPRLIST,x/cmp #BOXID0 (feeds adc #$FF, unchanged). lda dpass/adc/beq do not touch Y, so cpy #BOXID0+BOXN compares the same id the removed lda SPRLIST,x reloaded; bcc @write consumes the same C. After that the code is unchanged (ldy spi reloads Y before KEEP,y; @write sets Y itself; A at @write is not read before lda SPRLIST+1,x).
review: X and Y are not live into @l. Every path to @write reloads Y with ldy #1, the KEEP path reloads it with ldy spi, and @endpass/@next use neither. ldx sprmul5,y and ldy SPRLIST,x exist on the NMOS 6502. cpy #BOXID0 gives the same C into adc, and Y survives lda dpass/adc, so cpy #BOXID0+BOXN compares the same id. A is not read at @write before lda SPRLIST+1,x. Faster on every path. Scratch assemble: Master -4, Model B -4.

original: jmp @l
proposal: bne @l                      ; spi <= NSPR: never wraps to 0
cycles: jmp 3 -> bne taken 3, both targets (always taken).
assumption: Z is clear after inc spi at 1459: spi < NSPR on entry to the body (cpx NSPR/bcs @endpass at 1412-1413) and NSPR <= MAXSPR (32 / MAXSPRDEF) < 255, so inc gives 1..NSPR, never 0. Range: t_b.lst has jmp @l at $15A and @l at $F0 -> offset -108 (Model B), Master -107; other candidates only shrink it.
argument: inc spi sets Z only if spi became 0, which cannot happen, so bne is always taken to the same target the jmp reached.
review: spi < NSPR (unsigned) in the loop body, so spi <= 254 and inc spi never gives 0. Nothing else writes spi and it has no aliases. The bne is always taken, at 3 cycles like the jmp. In range on both targets by scratch assemble (Model B encodes D0 C0 alone). Saves 1 byte on each.

original:
dec dpass
        bmi :+
        jmp @pass                   ; (out of branch range on the 6502 build)
:       ldx curbuf
proposal:
dec dpass
        bpl @pass                   ; (in range on both builds)
:       ldx curbuf
cycles: second-pass path: dec + bmi not taken 2 + jmp 3 -> dec + bpl taken 3 (-2 cy); exit path: bmi taken 3 -> bpl not taken 2 (-1 cy). Both targets.
assumption: Branch range: Model B listing (build/grind/lst/t_b.lst) has @pass at $E2 and the bpl would sit at $160 with next PC $162: offset exactly -128, legal, and every other candidate here only shrinks it (-122 with all applied; verified by a scratch assemble); Master: @pass $4E8, next PC $563, offset -123. ca65 rejects an out-of-range branch, so a miscount cannot be silent.
anon_change: none: the ':' on 'ldx curbuf' is kept (now unreferenced) so the anonymous-label count is unchanged
argument: dec dpass sets N from the result; bmi :+ went to ldx curbuf when negative, else jmp @pass. bpl @pass branches on the opposite condition to the same target and falls through to ldx curbuf otherwise. No flag consumed after ldx curbuf.
review: bpl @pass is the exact inverse of bmi :+ over jmp @pass. The ':' stays, so the anonymous-label count is unchanged. Range checked by scratch assemble: on the Model B alone it encodes 10 80 (exactly -128, which is legal), and the offset gets smaller with the other candidates applied. Master is in range. Both paths are faster. Saves 3 bytes on each.

original:
stza spclip                 ; set at every window edge the sprite is cut against
        cmp #BOXID0+BOXN            ; the "nothing can disturb it" aliases draw the same
        bcc :+                      ; picture as the ids BOXN below them
        sbc #BOXN
:
        sta sp_id
        stza ptr+1
proposal:
.if MODELB
        ldx #0                      ; X is dead on entry (ldx spbank below)
        stx spclip                  ; set at every window edge the sprite is cut against
  .else
        stza spclip                 ; set at every window edge the sprite is cut against
  .endif
        cmp #BOXID0+BOXN            ; the "nothing can disturb it" aliases draw the same
        bcc :+                      ; picture as the ids BOXN below them
        sbc #BOXN
:
        sta sp_id
  .if MODELB
        stx ptr+1                   ; X = 0 still
  .else
        stza ptr+1
  .endif
cycles: Master: identical code. Model B: stza spclip (abs, LGCLOBSS: pha3+lda#2+sta4+pla4=13) + stza ptr+1 (zp: 12) = 25 cy -> ldx #0 2 + stx abs 4 + stx zp 3 = 9 cy.
assumption: X is not an input to drawsprite: its first X use is ldx spbank (engine.s:1490) and nothing between 1477 and 1490 reads X. Callers are draw_sprites (jsr at 1452; X not read afterwards, @next reloads) and the far entry F_DRAWSPR (farcall destroys X by contract, cpu.inc). spclip is absolute in bank 7 on the Model B (LGCLOBSS, engine.s:414); ptr is zp. N,Z after ldx/stx vs stza's pla: both overwritten by cmp #BOXID0+BOXN before any branch; C untouched by both.
argument: Both stza stores write 0 while keeping A = id; on the Model B, X=0 does the same without touching A. Between the two stores cmp/bcc/sbc/sta do not modify X, so stx ptr+1 still stores 0. ptr+1 is then shifted by rol as before. X is overwritten by ldx spbank at 1490.
review: X is not an input to drawsprite. Its first X use is ldx spbank; the callers are draw_sprites and the far/TOMAIN wrappers, and drawsprite overwrites X anyway. cmp/bcc/sbc/sta do not touch X, so stx ptr+1 stores 0. cmp overwrites the N,Z,C that either spelling sets. Master output is byte-identical. Model B LGCCODE is 6 bytes smaller (spclip is absolute in LGCLOBSS, ptr is zero page), and the stores drop from 25 to 9 cycles.

original:
bitimm 4
        beq :+
        bankimm ldx, (BANK_SPR|$80), BANK_LVL
:       bitimm $10              ; A still holds the flags byte
        beq :+
proposal:
.if MODELB
        lsr                         ; C = flags bit 2
        lsr
        lsr                         ; and bit 1 = flags bit 4
        bcc :+
  .else
        bitimm 4
        beq :+
  .endif
        bankimm ldx, (BANK_SPR|$80), BANK_LVL
:
  .if MODELB
        and #2
  .else
        bitimm $10              ; A still holds the flags byte
  .endif
        beq :+
cycles: Master identical. Model B: bitimm 4 (15 cy) + beq -> lsr x3 (6) + bcc: -9 cy; bitimm $10 (15) + beq -> and #2 (2) + beq: -13 cy. The taken/not-taken structure is the same.
assumption: A dead after the second test: at 1523-1524 'stx sp_dbank / lda sp_id' reloads A (the flags byte is also saved in sp_flags at 1515). Nothing reads mtmp without writing it first (only the cpu.inc macros use mtmp). C after 1522: the next C consumer follows asl at 1525, which overwrites it. The bankimm ldx sites keep their size and are recorded by their own @bf_ labels, which move with them.
anon_change: none: both ':' definitions stay outside the conditionals (the second is split onto its own line before the .if); each assembled arm has one :+ reference, as before
argument: Model B: A = flags (from lda (ptr),y at 1514). Three lsr put flags bit 2 in C and leave A = flags>>3, whose bit 1 is flags bit 4. bcc skips the SPR|$80 ldx exactly when bit 2 is clear, as bitimm 4/beq did. and #2 gives Z when flags bit 4 is clear, as bitimm $10 did. lsr/and do not touch X, so the ldx results reach stx sp_dbank unchanged. The Master assembles exactly the original.
review: On the Model B, after three lsr, C = flags bit 2 and A bit 1 = flags bit 4, so bcc/beq take the same paths as bitimm 4/beq and bitimm $10/beq. A is dead (lda sp_id follows stx sp_dbank), C is overwritten by asl, and neither form touches V. The bankimm sites are unchanged and sit outside the conditionals. The ':' count is unchanged. Master output is byte-identical. A scratch assemble shows Model B LGCCODE 11 bytes smaller, and it is faster.

original:
clc
  .if MODELB
        adc sprtab                  ; the directory sits above the map: where the
        sta ptr                     ; loader put it (low.s)
        lda ptr+1
        adc sprtab+1
        sta ptr+1
        jsr dirfetch                ; the directory is in bank 6: its eight bytes come
  .else                             ; into low RAM and ptr points there
        adc #<SPR_TABLE
proposal:
.if MODELB
        clc
        adc sprtab                  ; the directory sits above the map: where the
        sta ptr                     ; loader put it (low.s)
        lda ptr+1
        adc sprtab+1
        sta ptr+1
        jsr dirfetch                ; the directory is in bank 6: its eight bytes come
  .else                             ; into low RAM and ptr points there
        adc #<(SPR_TABLE-1)         ; C = 1 from the cpx (X = BANK_SPR): the -1 takes it back
        .assert <SPR_TABLE <> 0, error, "drawsprite: adc #<(SPR_TABLE-1) needs <SPR_TABLE nonzero"
cycles: Master: clc(2) removed, adc #imm 2->2: 2 cycles faster on the one path; Model B identical code
assumption: C = 1 on arrival (Master): the fall-through of `bankimm cpx, BANK_SPR, BANK_LVL / bne @titledir` (engine.s:1491-1492) means X = BANK_SPR, so cpx left C = 1; ldx #BANK_LVL / stx ROMSEL_CPY / stx ROMSEL (1494-1496) do not touch C. <SPR_TABLE is nonzero (labels.txt: SPR_TABLE = $A9C8); guarded by the added link-time .assert.
argument: Master: A + <(SPR_TABLE-1) + C(=1) = A + <SPR_TABLE exactly (as a 9-bit sum) whenever <SPR_TABLE >= 1, so the low byte and the carry into `adc #>SPR_TABLE` are identical. Model B: the clc just moves inside its own branch (it needs it: adc sprtab is a variable).
review: Text matches 1498-1507. Master: fall-through of cpx #BANK_SPR/bne means Z=1 so C=1; ldx/stx/stx and BANKREF (no code on Master) keep C. A+<(SPR_TABLE-1)+1 = A+<SPR_TABLE as a 9-bit sum when <SPR_TABLE>=1 ($C8 in labels.txt), guarded by the .assert. Model B: clc just moves into its arm. Master -1 byte, -2 cycles.

original:
ldy #6
        lda (ptr),y
proposal:
.if MODELB
        lda MAPBUF+6                ; dirfetch left ptr = MAPBUF
  .else
        ldy #6
        lda (ptr),y
  .endif
cycles: Model B: ldy#6(2)+lda (zp),y(5)=7 -> lda abs 4; Master unchanged
assumption: Model B: this point is reached only after `jsr dirfetch` (1505), which ends with ptr = MAPBUF (modelb/src/low.s:117-125; pagelogic, engine.s:4734, keeps A/X/Y/C and touches neither ptr nor MAPBUF). Y dead: the next Y reads are `ldaz ptr` at @entry2 (Model B: ldy #0 first) and ldy #7/ldy #4 later; the W=0 exit returns to draw_sprites (reloads Y: ldy spi / ldy #1) or draw_piece (menu.s:255, callers reload), and drawsprite already clobbers Y on every path.
argument: (ptr),6 with ptr = MAPBUF is MAPBUF+6: same byte, same N,Z; only Y (dead) differs.
review: Model B only reaches 1513 after jsr dirfetch (ptr=MAPBUF, low.s:121-124; pagelogic keeps regs). MAPBUF=$1DD absolute: lda abs 3 bytes vs ldy#/lda(zp),y 4. Y dead: next Y is ldaz(ldy #0)/ldy #7/#4; W=0 exit: callers (draw_sprites @next, draw_piece and its menu.s callers) never read Y.

original:
bitimm 4
        beq :+
        bankimm ldx, (BANK_SPR|$80), BANK_LVL
:       bitimm $10              ; A still holds the flags byte
        beq :+
proposal:
.if MODELB
        lsr
        lsr
        lsr                         ; C = flags bit 2
        bcc :+
  .else
        bitimm 4
        beq :+
  .endif
        bankimm ldx, (BANK_SPR|$80), BANK_LVL
:
  .if MODELB
        lsr
        lsr                         ; C = flags bit 4
        bcc :+
  .else
        bitimm $10                  ; A still holds the flags byte
        beq :+
  .endif
cycles: Model B: bitimm 4 (sta/and/php/lda/plp = 8 bytes, 15 cycles) -> 3 lsr = 6; bitimm $10 15 -> 2 lsr = 4; branches same cost on both arms. Master unchanged
assumption: A = sp_flags on entry (lda (ptr),y / sta sp_flags at 1514-1515; bankimm ldx leaves A). A dead after the second test: line 1523 `stx sp_dbank` then 1524 `lda sp_id`. mtmp's value (written by the old bitimm) is scratch owned by the macros, never read across.
anon_change: none: the `:` of line 1520 is kept (now on its own line) and the one at 1523 is untouched; the :+ references are inside mutually exclusive .if arms
argument: Model B: after 3 lsr C = old bit 2, so bcc skips exactly when (A & 4) = 0 (was beq after bit #4); two more lsr put old bit 4 in C, so bcc skips exactly when (A & $10) = 0. The bank-site ldx's (recorded instructions) are not moved or resized. X and the flags consumed later (none: stx, lda sp_id) are unchanged.
review: Text matches. Model B bitimm = sta mtmp($DF zp)/and/php/lda/plp = 8 bytes 15 cy; 3 lsr puts bit2 in C, bcc skips iff bit clear; bankimm ldx leaves A; 2 more lsr put bit4 in C. A dead (stx sp_dbank; lda sp_id), mtmp not read later. Anonymous count unchanged (single ':' kept, none inside .if arms). Bank-site ldx instructions unchanged. 5+6=11 bytes.

original: bra @entry2
proposal: bcc @entry2                 ; C = 0 from the asl: sp_id < 128
cycles: Model B: jmp 3 -> bcc taken 3; Master: bra 3 -> bcc taken 3
assumption: sp_id < 128 on this (game sprite) path: drawsprite folds ids >= BOXID0+BOXN (118) down by BOXN (1478-1480), the directory has 118 entries (SPR_TABLE is 944 bytes, ldprog.s:497 nt=118) and the Master's `lda SPRMASK,x` with x = 2*id already requires 2*id < 256. So `asl` at 1525 leaves C = 0, and tax / lda abs,x / sta do not touch C.
argument: The branch is always taken (C = 0), so it is an unconditional jump to @entry2; @entry2 is 62 bytes on (Model B listing $1D2->$213) - in range.
review: sp_id <= 117 (fold at BOXID0+BOXN=118; directory has 118 entries), so asl leaves C=0; tax/lda/sta keep C; bcc always taken. Master bra->bcc same size/cycles; Model B jmp(3)->bcc(2). Range fine (assembler would error otherwise).

original:
sta ptr                     ; only this path uses id*8 as the low byte unadjusted
        lda ptr+1
        clc

assumption: (1) C = 0 at lda tmp4. The preceding `lda sp / clc / adc wfine / sta sp` cannot carry: sp comes from ringaddr as a char address, whose low byte is 8-aligned (RINGLO/RING_A/RING_B are xx80, and ROWBYTES and the ringup folds are multiples of 8). wfine is 2/4/6 (see the @ftab dispatch and the bne at 2460). (2) tmp4 <= 79: 0 on the @all path, PART_LO,x on the other, where LO <= min(HI,79) because the sbc at 2476 did not borrow. (3) X is dead: ldx wfine at 2579 reloads it before any use. (4) ptr+1 is not read in between: the old intermediate stores only served the reload. Verified exhaustively in Python against the original fold, for every ringS in [0,RINGCHARS) and tmp4 in [0,79]: Master (2560 chars, base $3000) and Model B (1840 chars, base xx80, several ringbhi). Lines 2517-2520 (lda sp / clc / adc wfine / sta sp) must stay an adc: an `ora wfine` spelling there would leave C unknown here.
argument: Original: v = ringS + tmp4 + (RINGCHARS-80), minus RINGCHARS if v >= RINGCHARS; then ptr = v*8 + base, shifted in memory with asl/rol. New: d = ringS + tmp4 - 80. The low byte is tmp4 + $B0 (cannot carry, since tmp4 <= $4F) plus ringS; the high byte is ringS+1 + $FF + C. The carry out of adc #$FF is 1 exactly when d >= 0, which is exactly when the original folded (v - RINGCHARS = d). When d < 0 the code adds RINGCHARS, giving v: 16-bit on the Model B, high byte only on the Master, where <RINGCHARS = 0. The three shifts then keep the high byte in A (rol A instead of rol ptr+1): same bits, and the same final C = 0 since the offset is under $5000. The base add is the original's, with A or X holding the high byte. Final ptr/ptr+1, A, and the flags of the last adc are identical. X is clobbered on the Model B, where it is dead.
review: Original matches 2523-2574. C=0 at lda tmp4: sp is a char address (8-aligned, bases xx80) plus wfine in {2,4,6} (wy&3)*2, so there is no carry. tmp4 <= 79 on both paths, so tmp4+$B0 cannot carry, and the carry out of adc #$FF is exactly (ringS+tmp4 >= 80), which is exactly the original's fold condition v >= RINGCHARS, with v-RINGCHARS = d. The d<0 path adds RINGCHARS (16-bit on the Model B, high byte on the Master where <RINGCHARS = 0). rol A gives the same bits and final C=0 as rol ptr+1. The base add is identical and ptr+1 is not read in between. X is clobbered on the Model B only, and ldx wfine follows. Measured Master CODE -21, Model B TILCODE -30. Faster on every path. The gate passes with it applied (B title aside, see 0).

With Z = 0 at every arrival, the bne always goes to the patched @g4/@g2/@g0, exactly as the jmp did. Y, X and A at the targets are unchanged (A is overwritten by lda (sp),y).         txa

:       ldy #0

        sta (w16b),y
        iny
        cpy tmp2

proposal:
@bs:    ldy #1
        lda (w16),y                 ; offset high ($FF = end)
        cmp #$FF
        beq @bsdone
        tax                         ; X is free: the @bf counter ran down to 0
        ldaz w16                    ; offset low, (zp): Y stays 1
        clc
        adc #<(BARADDR-3)           ; dest - 3: the copy's Y runs 3..len+2, over the
        sta w16b                    ; header, so w16 needs no step past it
        txa
        adc #>(BARADDR-3)
        sta w16b+1
        iny                         ; Y = 2
        lda (w16),y
        adc #3                      ; C clear: no carry out of the high byte above
        sta tmp2                    ; len + 3
        iny                         ; Y = 3
@bc:    lda (w16),y
        sta (w16b),y
        iny
        cpy tmp2
        bne @bc
        tya                         ; step past the header and the data (Y = len + 3)
        clc
        adc w16
        sta w16
        bcc @bs
        inc w16+1
        bra @bs
@bsdone: rts
cycles: Master only. Terminator path: identical (ldy, lda, cmp, beq). Per span: ldy #2 -> iny (0cy); removed lda w16/clc/adc #3/sta w16/bcc (13cy, or 17 with the inc) and ldy #0 (2cy); added adc #3 (2) and iny (2). Net 11..15 cycles faster per span. The @bc loop body is unchanged (page crossings of the indexed modes may move; ignored per the brief). The step-past-data tail is unchanged.
assumption: Master only: the block is the .else of .if MODELB (lines 2681-2734). ldaz on the Master is lda (w16), which leaves Y = 1. BARADDR + offset + len < $10000 (BARADDR = $2B00, the bar is 5 pages, max offset in the data is 908), so the high-byte adc clears C before adc #3. Every span has len <= 252, so len+3 does not wrap: the span list built by tools/convert.py:1237-1248 into build/BOX currently has 20 spans, max len 39 (checked). w16, w16b and tmp2 are zero page (listing). tmp2 and X are not read after @bsdone (rts).
anon_change: Removes the `:` at line 2720 together with its only reference, the bcc :+ at 2718. No other anonymous reference crosses it: bar_bg has no other anonymous labels, blank_below's spnext resolves its :++ internally, and build_sections' first anonymous reference (beq :+ at 2770) points forward to 2772. The Model B does not assemble this block.
argument: Old: w16b = BARADDR + off; tmp2 = len; w16 += 3; copy (w16)+0..len-1 -> (w16b)+0..len-1; w16 += len. New: w16b = BARADDR - 3 + off (low add with C=0, high add with the low carry, so an exact 16-bit add); tmp2 = len + 3 (C = 0 from the high add); Y = 3; copy (w16)+3..len+2 -> (w16b)+3..len+2, i.e. source w16+3+k -> dest BARADDR+off+k for k = 0..len-1, exactly the old bytes. The loop exits with Y = len+3, so w16 += len+3, which equals the old +3 then +len; the same bcc/inc handles the carry into w16+1. A and X at exit do not matter because the loop back to @bs reloads them. iny replaces ldy #2 because Y = 1 from ldy #1 (lda (zp) on the 65C02 keeps Y). [Sizes verified by assembling a scratch copy of both targets with this change alone.]
review: Master-only block, original matches 2699-2733. On the 65C02 lda (w16) keeps Y=1, so iny gives 2; the high-byte adc of BARADDR-3+off leaves C=0, so adc #3 makes tmp2=len+3; the copy for Y=3..len+2 moves source w16+3+k to BARADDR+off+k, the same bytes as before, and exit Y=len+3 steps w16 past header and data in one add. The removed ':' at 2720 and its only reference bcc :+ at 2718 go together; no other anonymous reference crosses it (next is beq :+ at 2770 forward to 2772, no anon-emitting macros between). Precondition: every span len <= 252 (the old code allowed 255): the current span list in build/BOX (SPR_BAR=$BC60) has 20 spans, len 1..39, so it holds with a big margin. Assembled: Master CODE -11; Model B does not assemble it. 11-15 cycles faster per span, not timing-critical.

original:
lda rc_x
        sec
        sbc wcx
        sta w16
        lda rc_x+1
        sbc wcx+1
        sta w16+1
        bpl @right
        ; rel < 0: the visible width is w + rel, and rel is already two's complement,
        ; so add rather than negate-and-subtract.  Only a result whose high byte comes
        ; out exactly 0 survives: anything else is the whole rect off the left edge.
        lda w16
        clc
        adc rc_w
        sta rc_w
        beq @none                   ; Z is still the low sum: sta sets no flags
        lda w16+1
        adc #0                      ; branches do not touch C
        bne @none
        lda wcx
        sta rc_x
        lda wcx+1
        sta rc_x+1
        lda rc_w                    ; rel is now exactly 0, so the right clip is just
        cmp #ROWCHARS+1             ; min(rc_w, ROWCHARS): no need to store it and read
        bcc :+                      ; it back through the general test below
        lda #ROWCHARS
        sta rc_w
:       jmp drawrect
@right: lda w16+1
        bne @none                   ; rel >= 256 -> off right
        lda w16
        cmp #ROWCHARS
        bcs @none                   ; not taken: C = 0 for the adc
        adc rc_w
        cmp #ROWCHARS+1
        bcc :+                      ; not taken: C = 1 for the sbc
        lda #ROWCHARS
        sbc w16
        sta rc_w
:       jmp drawrect
proposal:
lda rc_x
        sec
        sbc wcx
        tay                         ; rel lo, kept in Y
        lda rc_x+1
        sbc wcx+1
        tax                         ; rel hi, kept in X (N,Z as the sbc left them)
        bpl @right
        ; rel < 0: the visible width is w + rel, and rel is already two's complement,
        ; so add rather than negate-and-subtract.  Only a result whose high byte comes
        ; out exactly 0 survives: anything else is the whole rect off the left edge.
        tya
        clc
        adc rc_w                    ; the low sum: the width, if it survives
        beq @none
        inx                         ; hi + C = 0 only for hi = $FF with a carry out
        bne @none
        bcc @none                   ; (inx and branches leave C alone)
        ldx wcx                     ; rel is now exactly 0, so the right clip is just
        stx rc_x                    ; min(width, ROWCHARS): the width is still in A
        ldx wcx+1
        stx rc_x+1
        cmp #ROWCHARS+1
        bcc :+
        lda #ROWCHARS
:       sta rc_w
        jmp drawrect
@right: bne @none                   ; Z from the tax: rel >= 256 -> off right
        tya
        cmp #ROWCHARS
        bcs @none                   ; not taken: C = 0 for the adc
        adc rc_w
        cmp #ROWCHARS+1
        bcc :+                      ; not taken: C = 1 for the sbc
        sbc #ROWCHARS               ; the excess e = lo + w - ROWCHARS (C stays 1)
        eor #$FF
        adc rc_w                    ; w - e = ROWCHARS - lo
        sta rc_w
:       jmp drawrect
cycles: Common prefix: sta w16/sta w16+1 (6) -> tay/tax (4). Right path: lda w16+1 is dropped (-3) and lda w16 -> tya (-1). The right clamp goes from lda #80/sbc w16 (5) to sbc #80/eor/adc rc_w (7), so right clamp is -4 net, right no-clamp -6, and the right @none exits are faster. Left path: lda w16 -> tya (-1); the sta rc_w before beq is removed (-3); lda w16+1/adc #0/bne (7) -> inx/bne/bcc (6); the lda rc_w reload is removed (-3); lda/sta wcx -> ldx/stx costs the same; the one sta rc_w after the clamp label replaces the pre-store. Every path is 2 to 11 cycles faster and no path is slower. Identical on both targets (no macros).
assumption: X and Y are dead at entry to drawrect_clip and at every exit. The callers: erase_old (engine.s ~1345-1365): after the call, @next never reads X or Y, @l reloads X from lidx and @erase loads Y. draw_dirty (engine.s ~3680): after the call, dec lcnt/bne @l, then @l does ldy lidx and the loop exit does ldx curbuf. On the Model B, bank5_entry (banks.s:158) does jmp drawrect_clip and returns through callbank -> jsr BANKENTRY / jmp pagelogic (low.s:131); pagelogic passes A, X and Y through untouched. drawrect (engine.s:563) writes X (tax, ldx curbuf, tax) and Y (ldy rc_nt) before reading them, and MIRDIRTY_BODY (banks.s:114) also writes X and Y before reading. w16 and w16+1 are no longer written here: drawrect writes w16+1 (engine.s:604) and w16 (engine.s:613) before ringaddr reads them, nothing in between reads them, and no caller reads w16 after drawrect_clip. rc_w is no longer written on the @none paths: every caller writes rc_w before each call (engine.s 1345, 3680), and only drawrect reads it. drawrect does not use C, A or the flags on entry (it starts with lda rc_h, then sec / cmp). wcx, rc_x and rc_w are all zero page, so ldx/stx zp work.
anon_change: None. The left path's ':' moves from the jmp drawrect line to the sta rc_w line just above it, so there is still one label between the two bcc :+ sites. The count is unchanged, and so is the right path's ':'.
argument: The low byte of rel is kept in Y (tay) instead of w16, and the high byte in X (tax) instead of w16+1. tax sets N and Z from the high byte exactly as the sbc did, so bpl @right and the new @right bne @none (which replaces lda w16+1/bne) test the same flags. Left path: tya gives lo, and adc rc_w gives the same low sum and carry; beq @none is unchanged. The original survives only if (hi + C) & 255 == 0 with hi in 80..FF, which means hi = FF and C = 1: inx/bne tests hi = FF and bcc tests C (inx does not touch C). The width stays in A, because ldx/stx move wcx into rc_x without touching A, so rc_w = min(sum, 80) is stored once after the clamp instead of being stored, reloaded and stored again. Right path: tya replaces lda w16. The clamp needs 80 - lo, which equals w - e where e = lo + w - 80. sbc #80 gives e: C = 1 from the failed bcc, and there is no borrow because A >= 81. eor #FF / adc rc_w with C = 1 then gives ~e + w + 1 = w - e, the same mod 256 as lda #80 / sbc w16. Checked exhaustively in C over every hi, lo and w (16.7M cases): the none/draw decision, rc_w and the rc_x update all match. Assembled in a scratch copy for both targets: drawrect_clip goes from 118 to 109 bytes on each.
review: Original matches engine.s 3392..3432 exactly. The scratch copy assembles and links on both targets: Master LOW goes from $B6 to $AD bytes and Model B TILCODE from $900 to $8F7, so 9 bytes are saved on each. An exhaustive C check over hi, lo and w (16.7M cases) matches the original on the draw/none decision, on rc_w when drawing and on the rc_x update. The right clamp is correct even when lo+w wraps past 255. X and Y are dead at every exit: erase_old's @next and @l, draw_dirty's loop (ldy lidx) and its exit (ldx curbuf), and pagelogic, which only writes them. drawrect writes X and Y before reading them and does not read flags, C or w16 on entry. w16 is written before it is read everywhere else, and rc_w is written by every caller before each call, so dropping those writes on the @none paths is harmless. The anonymous-label count is unchanged, there are no macros or bank sites here, and the code is not timing-critical. Cycles: every path is equal or faster (right clamp -4, right no-clamp -6, left paths -2 to -11).

        lda #BANK_MAP
        sta ROMSEL_CPY
        sta ROMSEL
        stz t16
        lda #>LV_MAP
        sta t16+1
        stz t16b                    ; row stride = 1 << maplw bytes
        stz t16b+1
        ldx maplw
        cpx #8
        beq :++
        lda #1
:       asl
        dex
        bne :-
        sta t16b
        bra :++
:       lda #1
        sta t16b+1
:       lda t16b                    ; (this ':' is counted by the beq/bra :++ above)
        sta MAPSTRIDE
        lda t16b+1
        sta MAPSTRIDE+1
        ldx #0
:       lda t16
        sta LV_MAPROWLO,x
        clc
        adc t16b
        sta t16
        lda t16+1
        sta LV_MAPROWHI,x
        adc t16b+1
        sta t16+1
        inx
        bne :-

proposal:
init_maprows:
        lda #BANK_MAP
        sta ROMSEL_CPY
        sta ROMSEL
        ldx maplw                   ; row stride = 1 << maplw bytes: lw = 8 shifts
        lda #1                      ; the 1 out into the carry, the high byte
:       asl
        dex
        bne :-
        sta t16b
        sta MAPSTRIDE
        txa                         ; (X = 0)
        rol
        sta t16b+1
        sta MAPSTRIDE+1
        ldy #<LV_MAP                ; Y = row address lo, A = hi, X = row
        lda #>LV_MAP
:       sta LV_MAPROWHI,x
        pha
        tya
        sta LV_MAPROWLO,x
        clc
        adc t16b
        tay
        pla
        adc t16b+1
        inx
        bne :-
        jmp pagelogic
cycles: Master only (LOW2), runs once per level. t16/t16b forward-referenced -> absolute. Row loop per iteration 41 -> 36 (x256 = -1280). Stride setup: lw=5..7 faster (45+(7lw-1) -> 27+(7lw-1)); lw=8 50 -> 84 (+34) but the loop's -1280 dominates, so every path through the routine is faster (lw=8 net -1250).
assumption: maplw is 1..8 (game.s:37 loops dex/bne on it, so never 0; widths 32..256 are 5..8); for lw=8 the last asl shifts $80 out into C with A=0, for lw<8 C=0 -- so txa (X=0 after the dex loop) / rol gives the high byte. Y and t16 are dead after the only caller: logic.s:443 level_init next does lda LV_HDR+2 / jsr @x8, and @x8 (logic.s:851) starts with tay; t16 is next written at logic.s:~502 before any read. The Model B stub (just rts) shows no shared code relies on t16/t16b from here. A at exit (the final hi after the last adc) and C/V are unchanged; pagelogic's pla gives N,Z from A as before; X = 0 as before.
anon_change: init_maprows' own ':' lines go from 4 to 2 (the two lw=8 special-case labels vanish with the beq/bra :++ that used them); every remaining reference (two bne :-) is inside the routine and still targets its loop head. No branch outside the routine counts across it: Master maprow/mapbyte/mapput above have no anonymous branches and build_tileaddr/getglyph below reference only their own labels.
argument: Stride: 1<<lw computed as a 9-bit shift (A low byte, C high byte) instead of the lw=8 special case; stored to t16b/t16b+1 and MAPSTRIDE as before. Row loop: hi in A, lo in Y instead of both in t16 (stack holds hi across the lo add); stores LV_MAPROWHI,x = hi and LV_MAPROWLO,x = lo before the add, then lo += t16b (C out) and hi += t16b+1 + C, identical to the original 16-bit add. Verified exhaustively in a Python model for lw 1..8 against LV_MAP + x*stride.
review: Original matches 4568-4604. Master-only, once per level. Stride: 9-bit shift of 1 by maplw (1..8; game.s:37 dex loop requires >=1) leaves low in A and the high bit in C; txa (X=0)/rol gives the high byte. Row loop: hi in A (stacked), lo in Y; stores then 16-bit add with carry preserved through tay/pla; LV_MAP=$8900 so <LV_MAP=0 matches the old stz t16. Exit A (last hi), C, X=0 and Z (from inx) identical into pagelogic (which preserves A/X/Y/C). Y dead: level_init next does lda LV_HDR+2 / jsr @x8 whose first instruction is tay. t16 is no longer left at its end value: the Model B stub never set it and the shared logic runs the same there, so nothing reads it. Anon labels 4->2, all refs internal; no outside branch counts across. Assembled: Master LOW2 481->449 (-32); Model B unchanged. Row loop 41->36 cy; lw=8 setup +34 but net -1250.

        sta t16
        lda #0
        rol
        sta t16+1
        lda t16

        sta t16b

        rol

@o3:    asl                         ; A = lo(6obj), C = bit 8
        sta t16
        rol t16+1                   ; = 4*seed + hi(6obj); C = 0
  .assert ((>LV_OBJS) & 3) < 2, error, "LV_OBJS: the seed needs a second inc"

  .endif

        cmp #MAXDWY+1
        bcc @cdone

        sta dpx

@up:    lda dpx                     ; dpx+1 is $FF on this arm, so neither the

proposal:
vy_step:
        ldx #0                      ; X = dpx+1, the sign extension
        lda vy                      ; C = the carry out of vy low + 128
        cmp #$80
        lda vy+1
        adc #0                      ; A = (vy + 128) >> 8
        bmi @up
        cmp #MAXDWY+1
        bcc @st
        lda #MAXDWY
@st:    sta dpx
        stx dpx+1
        rts
@up:    dex                         ; dpx+1 = $FF
        cmp #<-MAXDWY
        bcs @st
        lda #<-MAXDWY
        bcc @st                     ; C = 0 from the compare

New: 12 prefix + positive no clamp 3+2+3+3+3=14 / clamp 3+2+2+2+3+3=15 / negative no clamp 2+2+2+3+3+3=15 / clamp 2+2+2+2+2+3+3+3=19 (+6 rts). Every path ~30 cycles faster. Model B original stz is 5 not 3: still faster.

Callers read nothing of A or flags on return: player_dead's add16 starts with clc; player_update's bmi16 dpx is bit dpx+1. Original vy_step left X untouched, so this relies on X being dead, verified above. MAXDWY = 8 (engine.s:102/118).

argument: Original: dpx = hi(vy+128) (the 16-bit add's high byte stored to dpx), dpx+1 = $FF if its bit 7 else 0; the 'bne @cdn' was dead (dpx+1 is 0 on that arm). P is computed as ((2q6 + q6) << 3) mod 256, which is the same byte as 16p+8p (the clc before adc q6 kills the asl carry). N after the last asl is bit 7 of P, exactly what sx16 tested (and #$80), so dey = adding the $FF high byte of sx(P). clc (both paths) / adc t16 gives the low byte of T+P. bcc/iny carries into Y, and the clc on the iny path restores C=0 (on the bcc-taken path C is already 0). A:Y is then (H:T)+sx(P) mod 2^16, added to vx with one add (adc vx / tya / adc vx+1). Two mod-2^16 adds equal one add of the mod-2^16 sum. The ry cost adds to the rx pass cost in both versions, and that cost only fell. ry<=-8: 15 -> 13 (ry+7 unsigned >= $8007, so the high byte is nonzero). ry>=8: 29 -> 13 or 17. ry in range: 28 -> 16, then stz bactive is unchanged.
assumption: X = low byte of py-by (the tax at logic.s:1786) and it survives to the ry test: the only instructions in between are sbc/sta/txa/clc/adc/bcc/inc (1787-1795) and the new rx test, which touches only A. ry = (py-by)+8 exactly as 16 bits (1784-1795), so ry+7 = (py-by)+15 and low(ry+7) = X+15 mod 256. A and the flags are dead at @nocatch (1804 lda bcnt) and at stz bactive (Model B lda #0, as before). X on exit is unchanged from the original (still low(py-by)). @xin is a new cheap label; grep shows it is not used in player_update's scope. This is not timing-critical code. A brute-force check of both predicates over all 65536 values matches the original signed tests.
anon_change: Removes 4 anonymous labels (the placeholder ':' inside each ble16i/bge16i expansion). No reference crosses them: the nearest are bne :+ at 1779 (target 1781), bcc :+ at 1806 (target 1808) and bne :- at 1829 (target 1825). None of the references in 1600-1960 is :++ or :--.
argument: Signed 16-bit v is in [-7,7] iff v+7 mod 65536 is in [0,14], i.e. high(v+7)=0 and low(v+7)<15. cmp #$F9 sets C = (low >= $F9), which is the carry out of low+7; adc #0 then gives high(v+7) = v+1 + C. For rx, A=0 in only two cases. (rx+1=$FF, C=1): rx is -7..-1, in range, carry out of adc = 1, so bcs @xin. (rx+1=0, C=0): rx is 0..$F8, carry out 0, in range iff low<8 (cmp #8/bcs). Every other high byte is out of range and takes bne @nocatch. For ry, once high(ry+7)=0, low(ry+7) = (X+15) mod 256, which is < 15 iff X+15 wraps, iff X >= $F1 (cpx #$F1/bcc). This matches the four ble16i/bge16i tests exactly (they are exact signed compares via the $80 bias).

A brute force over all 65536 values of both the rx and the ry test (the ry test with X=(ry_lo-8)&255) matches signed -7..7 exactly. Every operand is zero page (bx $7F, by $81, bvy $85, t16 $D1, ry $B8, qx $BE, qy $C0), so nothing aliases, and storing qx early is safe because nothing between writes bx or qx. ldx #0 leaves C alone for adc #0, and the N flag from that adc is the same bit sx16's and #$80 tests. The commuted add16 has the same carry chain, and t16/t16+1 from sx16 are overwritten before anything reads them. For -3*bvy, asl t16 / rol A / tax replaces sta t16+1 / asl16 / lda t16+1 with the same carry in, and nothing reads t16+1 before the sta at 1860. lda bvy / asl sets C to bit 7, as cmp #128 does. X is 0 after the dex/bne loop and nothing writes X before the bpl, so bpl does what cmp #$80 / bcc did. sta qy/qy+1 replace mov16 qy,by: A, N, Z, C, V and X are all the same at jsr getaltitude, which starts with jsr getinfo and does not read flags. The anonymous labels stay at 3, in the same order. The assembled listing differs only inside the range, and the new branch offsets resolve correctly. Every path is faster on both targets. Scratch build: Master LOGIC $2564 -> $254C (24 bytes); Model B LGCCODE $2A0A -> $29EE (28 bytes with the two stz candidates, i.e. 24+2+2).

; range check: rx > lo && rx < hi && ry > lo2 && ry < hi2 ; X = offset of the limit
; quad in RNGTAB (limits stored +128 so the test is an unsigned byte compare on r^$80,
; after checking r fits in -128..127 - anything wider fails every limit anyway).
; Returns carry set if inside. Clobbers A, X.
inrange:
        lda rx+1
        inca                         ; $FF -> 0, 0 -> 1, anything else >= 2
        cmp #2
        bcs @no
        lda rx
        eor rx+1                    ; low byte sign must agree with the high byte
        bmi @no
        lda rx
        eor #$80
        cmp RNGTAB,x
        bcc @no
        beq @no                     ; rx > lo
        cmp RNGTAB+1,x
        bcs @no                     ; rx < hi
        lda ry+1
        inca
        cmp #2
        bcs @no
        lda ry
        eor ry+1
        bmi @no
        lda ry
        eor #$80
        cmp RNGTAB+2,x
        bcc @no
        beq @no
        cmp RNGTAB+3,x
        bcs @no
        sec
        rts
@no:    clc
        rts

original:
sta t16
        lda obj
        asl
        asl
        asl
        sec
        sbc obj
        clc
        adc t16
proposal:
sta t16
        lda obj
        asl
        asl
        asl                         ; 8*obj: mod 16 only bit 3 is left, so eor adds it
        eor t16
        sec
        sbc obj                     ; q + 8*obj - obj = q + 7*obj (mod 16)
cycles: 22 -> 20 both targets
assumption: Only A & 15 is used: `and #15` follows at 2786, then tax/lda batoff,x; C after and #15 not consumed (clc at @wy1, and the bpl path has no carry use). t16 still = q.
argument: Let a = (8*obj) mod 256: its low nibble is 8*(obj&1). q XOR a agrees with q + a in bits 0-3 (flipping bit 3 = adding 8 mod 16). Subtraction's low nibble depends only on the operands' low nibbles, so ((q^a) - obj) & 15 = (a - obj + q) & 15, the original value (checked exhaustively over q, obj 0..255). sec/sbc obj keeps the exact -obj. (Also contained in the 2710-2805 kill-restructure candidate; this is its stand-alone form.)
review: Low nibble of (8*obj) xor q equals that of q + 8*obj (bits 0-2 of 8*obj clear); subtraction's low nibble depends only on low nibbles; only A&15 used, C/V after not consumed (clc at @wy1). Subsumed by 0.

original:

proposal:

        lda #8

cycles: jsr addscore(6) + return to @kill(6) + rts(6) -> jmp addscore(3) + bar_touch's rts straight to @kill's caller(6): 9 fewer, both targets
assumption: addscore (logic.s:2142) and bar_touch (logic.s:3223) touch only A, score, BARDIRTY and the flags, not fa, fe or SFXREQ, so the stores can go in any order. No stack inspection: plain jsr/jmp in the same segment. @kill's two callers (logic.s:2710, 2726) reload A after jsr @kill, so returning A=1 instead of SFX_KILL does not matter. DBGHIT/DBGTILE builds return at addscore's rts, with the same effect
argument: Do the stores first, then lda #6 / jmp addscore. addscore's rts (through jmp bar_touch) returns to @kill's caller. X and Y are untouched either way. py65 equivalence-tested on both CPUs.
review: Tail call is sound: addscore/bar_touch touch only A, score, BARDIRTY and flags; callers 2710/2725 reload A; no stack inspection, same segment, rts not a branch target. DBGHIT/DBGTILE early rts returns equally.

original:
lda fb                      ; t16 = fb + 256: only the high byte changes
        sta t16
        lda fb+1
        inca
        sta t16+1
        blt16 fd, t16, :+
        jmp @done
