proposal:
lda fb                      ; exit unless fd < t16 = fb + 256 (signed), tested
        clc                         ; as t16 - fd - 1 >= 0, so t16 is never stored
        sbc fd                      ; (t16's low byte is fb's own)
        ldx fb+1                    ; t16+1 = fb+1 + 1: ldx/inx/txa keep the carry
        inx
        txa
        sbc fd+1
        bvc :+
        eor #$80
:       bmi @done
cycles: Before the high-byte sbc: Master 20 -> 15, Model B 29 -> 15 (inca is 11 there). Continue path: bmi taken 3 -> bmi not taken 2. Exit path: bmi not taken 2 + jmp 3 -> bmi taken 3. Every path faster on both
assumption: X dead through @dead: the path ends in jmp m_addsprite (addsprite does ldx NSPR, engine.s:1382) or rts to process_object. Its continuation (logic.s:1985 setbank/ldy obj) and callers (logic.s:1059-1062 ldx bent; 1100-1102 inc BINI/bra/ldx BINI) reload X. t16 is a transient temp: the original fall-through overwrote it (sx16) before any read, and nothing after process_object reads t16 before writing it
anon_change: -1: the explicit ':' at line 2814 goes, along with blt16's forward reference to it. The one ':' left is the macro's own bvc target, spelled out. No branch counts across line 2814: there is no ':-' in logic.s 2740-3060, and the references at 2750-2752 resolve before it
argument: blt16 fd, t16 tests fd < t16 (signed), with t16 = fb + 256 and t16+1 = fb+1 + 1 mod 256. The new code computes t16 - fd - 1 as a 16-bit subtract: clc/sbc fd on the low byte (t16's low byte is fb), then (fb+1 + 1) - fd+1 - borrow. N^V (bvc/eor #$80) is the true sign of t16 - fd - 1, which is negative exactly when fd >= t16. So bmi @done exits exactly where the original reached jmp @done, and every other case falls into add16i, as the original's taken bmi :+ did. py65-verified on both CPUs, including fd = fb+256+{-2..2} and fb+1 = $7F/$FF wraps.
review: Computes t16-fd-1 as a 16-bit subtract (fb low, fb+1 +1 high); N^V negative exactly when fd >= t16. Spot-checked 200k cases incl. wraps in Python. X dead: process_object's staged path does not read X after @call, callers reload X, addsprite loads X first. t16 never read afterwards on either path. Anonymous -1 crosses no reference (no ':-' in logic.s 2800-3160). bmi @done in range (listing offset $5C).

original:
add16i fa, 120
        lda fa                      ; want only the high byte of fa + 128
        cmp #$80                    ; C = carry out of fa_lo + 128
        lda fa+1
proposal:
clc                         ; add16i fa, 120, keeping the new low byte in X
        lda fa
        adc #120
        sta fa
        tax
        lda fa+1
        adc #0
        sta fa+1                    ; want only the high byte of fa + 128:
        cpx #$80                    ; C = carry out of fa_lo + 128
cycles: add16i 20 + tax 2 + cpx 2 = 24, vs add16i 20 + lda 3 + cmp 2 + lda 3 = 28; both targets
assumption: X dead: jmp m_addsprite follows and nothing between reads X. The adc #0 kept at line 2819 consumes A = new fa+1 and C
argument: add16i is expanded in place with tax after the low store, so X = new fa_lo. After sta fa+1, A = new fa+1, exactly as the original's lda fa+1 reloaded it. cpx #$80 gives C = (fa_lo >= $80), as cmp #$80 on A = fa_lo did. N and Z differ before adc #0, but adc rewrites them.
review: add16i expanded with tax after the low store; cpx #$80 gives the same C; A = new fa+1 for the kept adc #0. X dead (only later X use is candidate 4's own tax).

original:
sx16 t16
        add16 fd, t16
proposal:
bpl :+                      ; fd += A sign-extended (N from the adc): pre-borrow
        dec fd+1                    ; the high byte when A is negative
:       clc
        adc fd
        sta fd
        bcc @fdok
        inc fd+1
@fdok:
cycles: Original 31/32. New, A positive: 14 (18 with a carry). A negative: 21 (25 with a carry). Both targets
assumption: N at line 2820 is A's sign, set by the adc #0 at line 2819. t16 and t16+1 are dead after: t16+1 is rewritten at line 2825 before any read, and t16 is never read again
anon_change: 0: sx16's internal ':' goes and one ':' is added before clc, so the count is unchanged. The second label is the cheap label @fdok. No reference counts across either
argument: fd += sign-extend(A). The low byte adds A; the high byte adds $FF when A is negative (the dec) plus the carry (bcc/inc). Identical to sx16 t16 / add16 fd, t16 for every A and fd (py65, both CPUs). The flags after differ, but lda fc+1 follows.
review: bpl on N from adc #0; dec/adc/bcc/inc is fd += sext(A) exactly; t16 no longer written but never read afterwards. @fdok unique in ob_bat scope; anon count unchanged, no crossing refs.

original:
sta t16+1
        lda fc
        ror a
        clc
        adc spx
        sta spx
        lda spx+1
        adc t16+1
proposal:
tax                         ; the high half waits in X (dead: addsprite loads it)
        lda fc
        ror a
        clc
        adc spx
        sta spx
        txa
        adc spx+1
cycles: sta 3 -> tax 2; lda 3 -> txa 2: 2 fewer, both targets
assumption: X dead on this path: it ends in jmp m_addsprite and nothing between reads X. t16+1 dead: only these lines read it
argument: The high half of fc>>1 waits in X instead of t16+1. tax and txa leave C, so ror a still takes C from the first ror. spx+1 + hi + C = hi + spx+1 + C: same result and same carry.
review: tax/txa preserve C for the second ror and the adc; addition commutes. X dead through jmp m_addsprite.

original:

        lda fd
        ror a
        clc
        adc spy
        sta spy
        lda spy+1
        adc t16+1

tax                         ; the high half waits in X, as above
        lda fd
        ror a
        clc
        adc spy
        sta spy
        txa
        adc spy+1
cycles: 2 fewer, both targets
assumption: X dead: bgt16 and jmp m_addsprite follow, and neither reads X. t16+1 dead after
argument: Same as the fc block, for fd into spy.
review: Same as index 4 for fd/spy; bgt16 and jmp m_addsprite do not read X.

original: bra :++
proposal: bne :++                     ; always: Z = 0 from the lda #65
cycles: Master bra 3 -> bne 3 at the same size; Model B jmp 3 -> bne 3 (page crossing aside)
assumption: None outside the window: Z = 0 from lda #65 on the line before
argument: lda #65 clears Z, so the branch is always taken to the same ':'. Anonymous count unchanged.
review: lda #65 sets Z=0 and the line is reached only by fall-through. Model B jmp->bne.

original:
inca
        sta q1                      ; step 1 or 2
        lda fc
        bne @left
        lda fb                      ; walking right.  fb can be -1 coming in (the left
        clc                         ; path rests one past the near end), and the carry
        adc q1                      ; out of the add is what clears its sign byte -- drop
        sta fb                      ; that and -1 + 2 becomes -255, not 1.
        bcc :+
        inc fb+1
:       cmp fa                      ; past here fb+1 is 0 and fb is 0..194, so the
        bcc @coll                   ; unsigned compare says what the signed 16-bit did
        lda #1
        sta fc
        bra @coll
@left:  lda fb
        sec
        sbc q1
proposal:
sta q1                      ; frame & 1: the step is q1 + 1, the + 1 the carry's
        lda fc
        bne @left
        lda fb                      ; walking right.  fb can be -1 coming in (the left
        sec                         ; path rests one past the near end), and the carry
        adc q1                      ; out of the add is what clears its sign byte -- drop
        sta fb                      ; that and -1 + 2 becomes -255, not 1.  (sec: the + 1)
        bcc :+
        inc fb+1
:       cmp fa                      ; past here fb+1 is 0 and fb is 0..194, so the
        bcc @coll                   ; unsigned compare says what the signed 16-bit did
        inc fc                      ; fc = 0 here (bne @left fell through): now 1
        bne @coll                   ; always
@left:  lda fb
        clc                         ; fb - q1 - 1: the step (C = 0 is the - 1)
        sbc q1
cycles: Master: inc a (2) gone; lda #1/sta (5) -> inc fc (5); bra 3 -> bne 3. Model B: inca (11) gone; jmp 3 -> bne 3. Every path faster or equal
assumption: q1 dead after ob_walker: it is read only here, and every other reader writes it first (logic.s 1586, 2207, 2296, 2579, 2629, 2749, 3073, 3261/3289; inrange, player_hit, boomready and boomrel never read it). fc's low byte = 0 on the right path, since bne @left fell through and nothing writes fc before
argument: q1 = frame&1 instead of (frame&1)+1. Right path: sec/adc q1 = fb + old q1, so A, carry-out (the sign-byte fix-up), N and Z are the same. Left path: clc/sbc q1 = fb - old q1, with C = 1 exactly when fb >= old q1, so the borrow, Z and N are the same. inc fc takes fc from 0 to 1 and clears Z, so bne always branches.
review: q1 only read within ob_walker here; every other q1 reader writes it first (mapbyte, 2207/2296 before star_safe/tramp_safe, 3073, div10, level init). sec/adc q1 and clc/sbc q1 give identical A, C, N, Z to the old step. fc low is 0 on the right path so inc fc = 1 with Z=0.

original:
bcs :+                      ; borrow == fb went negative: that IS the bmi16 test
        dec fb+1
        bra @stop
:       bne @coll                   ; Z still from the sbc, so fb's own load is not needed
@stop:  stz fc
proposal:
beq @stop                   ; fb reached 0 (a borrow never leaves zero: >= 254)
        bcs @coll                   ; no borrow, not zero: still walking
        dec fb+1                    ; borrow == fb went negative: that IS the bmi16 test
@stop:  stz fc
cycles: Borrow 10 -> 9; became zero 5 -> 3; otherwise 6 -> 5. Both targets
assumption: The step is 1 or 2, so a borrow leaves fb >= 254: C = 0 implies Z = 0. Z and C come from the sbc (sta fb keeps them). @stop has no other referrer
anon_change: -1: the ':' at 2885 goes with its only reference, bcs :+ at 2882. There is no ':-' in 2740-3060, and no forward reference counts across 2885
argument: The sbc has three outcomes. Borrow: dec fb+1, then @stop. No borrow and zero: @stop. No borrow and non-zero: @coll. The original reaches the same targets; beq only ever catches the zero case.
review: Borrow with step 1..2 leaves 254/255, so C=0 implies Z=0; all three outcomes map to the same targets. @stop has no other referrer; removed ':' crosses no reference.

original:
mov16 rx, sx
        mov16 ry, sy
proposal:
sta ry+1                    ; A = sy+1: boomrel's last store
        lda sy
        sta ry
        mov16 rx, sx
cycles: lda sy+1 removed: 3 fewer, both targets
assumption: boomrel (logic.s:2127) ends dif16 sy, spy, by (lda spy+1 / sbc by+1 / sta sy+1) and then rts, so A = sy+1 on return on both targets
argument: The same four bytes are written, ry+1 first from A. Nothing reads them in between.
review: boomrel ends with sta sy+1 (A = sy+1) then rts, on both targets (direct jsr, same file). Flags after are overwritten by ldx #44.

original:
blt16 fb, fa, :+
        bra @bset
:       stz fc
        bra @bset
proposal:
bge16 fb, fa, @bset
  .if ::MODELB
        lda #0                      ; (stz's own expansion, spelled out for its Z)
        sta fc
        beq @bset                   ; always
  .else
        stz fc
        bra @bset
  .endif
cycles: fb >= fa: 5 -> 3. fb < fa: bmi 3 -> bpl 2, then the same stz and a 3-cycle branch
assumption: A dead after: @bset does lda #8. On the Model B, Z = 1 from the lda #0
anon_change: -1: the ':' at 2911 goes; blt16/bge16's internal ':' stays. Nothing counts across 2911
argument: bge16 is the same compare as blt16, with bpl in place of bmi, so it folds the bra. On the Model B, stz is spelled out so the lda #0 sets Z for a 2-byte beq in place of the 3-byte jmp.
review: bge16 is blt16 with bpl: fb>=fa goes straight to @bset; else fc=0 then @bset. Model B lda #0 sets Z for beq. A dead at @bset (lda #8). Macro-internal ':' retained; removed ':' crosses nothing.

cycles: fe >= 9: 7 -> 5. @f0/@f2/@f8: 3 -> 3. Page crossing aside
assumption: @f0 and @f2 are reached only by bcc (lines 2928, 2930), so C = 0 there. The lda #6 arm is reached only when cmp #9's bcc falls through, so C = 1. @f8 loads 8, so Z = 0. The carry at @sp is dead: cpx or clc rewrites it
argument: lda #5 with C = 1 gives adc fc = 6 + fc, the same sum, carry, N and Z as lda #6 / clc / adc fc. Each bra becomes a branch on a flag that is proven at that point.
review: C at each site proven: lda #6 arm reached only on cmp #9 fall-through (C=1), @f0/@f2 only via bcc (C=0), @f8 loads 8 (Z=0). 5+fc+1 == 6+fc+0 in result and C.

original:
@sp:    ldx otype                   ; the frame stays in A: no round trip through q1
        cpx #5
        bne :+
        adc #66                     ; C = 1 from the equal cpx, so this is A + 67
        bra :++
:       clc
        adc #76
:       jmp m_addsprite
cycles: 12 on both otypes -> 9 (+1 if the table straddles a page). Both targets
assumption: otype is 5 or 6: ob_walker is reached only through @tab entries 5 and 6 (logic.s:2036), with otype = O_TYPE,y (logic.s:1933). The flags after are dead
anon_change: -2: both ':' (lines 2949, 2951) go with their only references. No ':-' up to line 3060
argument: Adds 67 (otype 5) or 76 (otype 6) through a 2-byte table in the code segment. The byte savings are net of the table.
review: otype is only 5 or 6 in ob_walker (dispatch @tab entries 5/6; otype written only by process_object, level init, and the DBGHIT kill-tile path outside the walk). Table is read from the executing segment. Assembled both targets with all 14 applied: every byte outside the region identical; Master LOGIC 9572->9530 (-42), Model B LGCCODE 10762->10698 (-64), matching the claimed sums.

original:
lda fe
        cmp #3
        bcc @f0
        cmp #6
        bcc @f2
        cmp #9
        bcc @f4
        lda #6
        clc                         ; only this arm reaches @fr with C set (cmp #9
        bra @fr                     ; fell through); @f2 and @f4 got here on a bcc
@f0:    lda fc
        bra @sp
@f2:    lda #2
        bra @fr
@f8:    lda #8
        bra @sp
@f4:    lda #4
@fr:    adc fc
@sp:    ldx otype                   ; the frame stays in A: no round trip through q1
        cpx #5
        bne :+
        adc #66                     ; C = 1 from the equal cpx, so this is A + 67
        bra :++
:       clc
        adc #76
:       jmp m_addsprite
proposal:
ldx fe                      ; fe in X, so each arm can load its frame early
        cpx #3
        bcc @f0
        cpx #6
        bcc @f2
        cpx #9
        lda #4
        bcc @fr                     ; C = 0: fc + 4
        lda #5                      ; C = 1 (cpx #9 fell through): fc + 6
@fr:    adc fc
@sp:    ldx otype                   ; the frame stays in A: no round trip through q1
        cpx #6                      ; otype is 5 or 6 (the walker's two table entries)
        bne :+                      ; 5: C = 0 from the cpx
        adc #8                      ; 6: C = 1, so A + 9, and C = 0 again
:       adc #67
        jmp m_addsprite
@f0:    lda fc                      ; C = 0: the bcc
        bcc @sp
@f2:    lda #2                      ; C = 0: the bcc
        bcc @fr
@f8:    lda #8
        bne @sp
cycles: fe<3: 14->14; 3..5: 20->20; 6..8: 21->21; >=9: 25->22; @f8: 5->5 (lda 2 + bne 3 = lda 2 + bra/jmp 3). Tail otype 5: 12->10, otype 6: 12->11. Model B identical (bra=jmp is 3 cycles, same as the taken branches).
assumption: otype is 5 or 6 here: ob_walker is entries 5 and 6 of process_object's @tab (logic.s:2036) and nothing in ob_walker writes otype (inrange, player_hit, boomready, boomrel checked; only DBGHIT's tile-kill path writes otype and it does not reach here). fc+8 < 247 (A+76 is a sprite number, so A < 180), so adc #8 with C=1 cannot carry. X dead on entry to the chain: @sp reloads it with ldx otype on every path. addsprite (engine.s:1381) reads neither X nor C nor V on entry (ldx NSPR first), and the handler's return goes to process_object's setbank (A,flags dead). @f8 is reached only from the bmi16/beq/bcs above (lines 2920-2924); its new place after the jmp is ~50 bytes away, in branch range.
anon_change: Removes one anonymous label: the original has ':' at 2949 (clc) and 2951 (jmp); the new has one (adc #67). The only references to them are the bne :+ / bra :++ inside this block; the nearest anonymous labels outside are 2911 (referenced by 2909's blt16) and 2996 (ob_spike's bcc :+), neither counts across this block. Verified by assembling: builds clean.
argument: Frame chain: X=fe; cpx sets C exactly as cmp did. fe<3 -> @f0: A=fc, C=0 -> bcc @sp (was bra). 3..5 -> @f2: A=2, C=0 -> bcc @fr: fc+2. 6..8: lda #4 (C kept from cpx #9 = 0) -> bcc @fr: fc+4 (was bcc @f4 / lda #4). >=9: C=1, lda #5 falls into @fr: 5+fc+1 = fc+6 (was lda #6 / clc / bra @fr). @f8: lda #8 leaves Z=0 so bne = bra. Tail: original otype 5: cpx #5 equal -> adc #66 with C=1 = A+67; otype 6: clc/adc #76 = A+76. New: cpx #6: otype 5 -> C=0, Z=0 -> adc #67 = A+67; otype 6 -> C=1, Z=1 -> adc #8 (+9, C=0) then adc #67 = A+76. A, N, Z identical at m_addsprite; X = otype as before. Verified in a scratch tree: all 12 candidates applied together assemble on both targets (measured savings 35 Master / 59 Model B LGCCODE), tools/gate.sh passes everything except 'B title', which fails identically for a trivial 1-byte shrink alone (a disc-size timing artifact, not this code); bdiff lock-step OK on all 16 levels.
review: Original matches. otype is 5/6 only (ob_walker is @tab entries 5,6; nothing in the handler writes otype outside DBGHIT's non-reaching path). Frame chain: cpx sets C as cmp did; 6..8: lda #4 keeps C=0 -> fc+4; >=9: C=1, lda #5 -> fc+6; @f0/@f2 reached on bcc so C=0; @f8 lda #8 Z=0 so bne always. Tail: cpx #6: otype 5 -> C=0 -> adc #67; otype 6 -> C=1, adc #8 (+9, no carry since fc is 0/1) then adc #67 = +76. A/N/Z/C/V at m_addsprite identical, X = otype. @f8 within range. Anonymous labels: 2949/2951 only referenced within block; blt16 at 2909 targets 2911, ob_spike's bcc :+ forward, no :- before 3202. Cycles no worse on any path. Scratch build: all 12 applied assemble on both; Master LOGIC -35, Model B LGCCODE -59, matching the claimed totals.

original:
lda health
        beq @draw
        lda fa
        bmi @draw                   ; still dormant
        cmp #8
        bcs @draw
proposal:
ldx health                  ; A = fa on both ways in, and ldx keeps it
        beq @draw
        cmp #8                      ; unsigned: a dormant (negative) fa is >= 8 too
        bcs @draw
cycles: health=0: 6->6; health!=0 & fa<0: 11->10; health!=0 & 8<=fa<128: 15->10; health!=0 & fa<8: 14->9. Same on Model B.
assumption: A = fa at @nowrap on both ways in: the fall-through from 'lda fa / cmp #24 / bne @nowrap' (cmp does not write A) and the wrap path ending 'sta fa'. X dead: the proceed path does ldx #48 before inrange; the @draw paths end in m_addsprite (addsprite does ldx NSPR first) or @done rts, and process_object's callers never read X after the handler (logic.s:1983 setbank/ldy obj; 1059 setbank; 1100 inc BINI/ldx BINI).
argument: lda health/beq -> ldx health/beq: same Z, A kept = fa. 'lda fa / bmi @draw / cmp #8 / bcs @draw' -> 'cmp #8 / bcs @draw': the unsigned compare sends 128..255 (negative) and 8..127 to @draw alike, so the bmi was only a fast path; it is now faster still since the reload is gone. Fall-through: A = fa in 0..7, C = 0, exactly as before.
review: A = fa at @nowrap on both entries (fall-through after cmp #24, and after sta fa). ldx health keeps A and gives same Z. Unsigned cmp #8 sends negatives (>=128) to @draw exactly like bmi did. Fall-through A=fa 0..7, C=0 as before. X changed to health on the @draw path, but X is dead: @draw reloads A, ends in addsprite (ldx NSPR) or rts to process_object staged path (setbank/ldy/lda) whose callers (logic.s:1059 ldx bent, 1100 ldx BINI) reload X. Cycles 6->6, 11->10, 15->10, 14->9.

original:
inca                        ; A is still fa: cmp does not write A
        asl
        eor #$80                    ; biased limit
proposal:
asl                         ; fa < 8 and C = 0 (bcs fell through): 2fa, C = 0
        adc #130                    ; (fa+1)*2 biased by $80
cycles: Master 6->4; Model B 15 (inca 11 + asl 2 + eor 2) -> 4.
assumption: C = 0 and A = fa in 0..7 on arrival: the preceding 'cmp #8 / bcs @draw' fell through (true with or without the ldx health candidate). V after is not read: next is sta RNGTAB+49 / ldx #48 / jsr inrange, which starts with lda rx+1 and never reads V or C.
argument: Original: A=fa (0..7) -> inc a -> fa+1 -> asl -> 2fa+2 (C=0) -> eor #$80 -> 2fa+130. New: asl -> 2fa, C=0 (bit 7 of fa is 0) -> adc #130 -> 2fa+130, no carry (<=144). N=1, Z=0, C=0 as before. On the Model B inca also wrote mtmp, scratch owned by the expansions (always written before read).
review: C=0, A=fa in 0..7 after the cmp #8/bcs fall-through. asl -> 2fa, C=0; adc #130 -> 2fa+130 (<=144), C=0, N=1, V=0: same A/N/Z/C as inca/asl/eor #$80. inrange starts lda rx+1/inca/cmp and never reads incoming C or V. Master 4->3 bytes, Model B 9->3 (inca is 6).

original:
lda #23
        sec
        sbc fa
cycles: Master and Model B: 7 -> 4 on the fa>=8 path.
assumption: A = fa at this point (lda fa / bmi / cmp #8 / bcc: cmp does not write A) and C = 1 (bcc not taken). fa <= 23 at @draw: fa is incremented to 24 only to be replaced by a negative value in the same call (lines 2958-2967), and negatives leave at bmi @done.
argument: lda #23 / sec / sbc fa = 23-fa with C=1 (no borrow). eor #$FF gives 255-fa; adc #23 with C=1 gives 279-fa = 256 + (23-fa): A = 23-fa and C=1 since fa<=23. Same A, N, Z, C, and V irrelevant (lsr/clc/adc #85 follow; adc overwrites V).
review: A = fa (lda fa/bmi/cmp #8), C=1 on fall-through. eor #$FF/adc #23 with C=1 computes 23 + ~fa + 1, the exact operation sbc does for 23-fa: identical A, N, Z, C and V for every fa. 5->4 bytes, 7->4 cycles both targets.

original:
:       lda fe
        clc
        adc #93
proposal:
:       lda fe
        adc #93                     ; C = 0: process_object's asl of otype (9) before the dispatch
cycles: Both paths 2 cycles faster on both targets.
assumption: C = 0 at ob_flame's entry: it is reached only through process_object's @tab (logic.s:2036-2037; grep finds no other reference), and type 9 >= NLEAN(2) goes through the @gen path, which ends 'lda otype / asl / tax / jsr @call' (logic.s:1980-1983): asl of 9 clears C. @call is 'jmpx @tab': jmp (abs,x) on the Master, and on the Model B pha/lda/sta/lda/sta/pla/jmp (jv), none of which writes C. Nothing in ob_flame before here writes C (lda, and, bne, inc, sta).
argument: The clc was redundant: C is provably 0 at the adc #93 on both paths (bne-taken and inc path).
review: ob_flame is referenced only from process_object @tab; type 9 >= NLEAN goes through the staged path 'lda otype/asl/tax/jsr @call': asl of 9 leaves C=0; jmpx (jmp (abs,x) on Master; pha/lda/sta/lda/sta/pla/jmp (jv) on Model B) and lda/and/bne/inc/sta in ob_flame do not touch C. clc is redundant on both paths.

original:
lda #1
        sta fa
proposal: inc fa                      ; fa was 0: bne @adv fell through
cycles: 5 -> 5 on both (lda #imm 2 + sta zp 3 = inc zp 5).
assumption: fa = 0 here: 'lda fa / bne @adv' fell through, and neither the health checks nor inrange (logic.s:2065, reads rx/ry/RNGTAB only) write fa. fa is zero page ($AC). A and flags are overwritten by the following lda #3.
argument: inc of 0 stores 1, as lda #1 / sta fa did.
review: fa = 0 on this path (lda fa/bne @adv fell through); lda health/cmp and inrange (reads rx/ry/RNGTAB only) do not write fa; fa is zp $AC. inc fa stores 1; A and N/Z are overwritten by lda #3, C untouched by either form. 4->2 bytes, 5->5 cycles.

original: bra @draw
proposal: bne @draw                   ; Z = 0: SFX_POWER is 6
cycles: 3 -> 3 (taken branch vs bra/jmp).
assumption: SFX_POWER = 6 (logic.s:3313), so the preceding lda #SFX_POWER leaves Z = 0; sta does not change flags.
argument: Branch always taken, same target.
review: SFX_POWER = 6 (logic.s:3313): lda #SFX_POWER leaves Z=0 and sta SFXREQ keeps it, so bne is always taken to the nearby @draw. Master 2->2, Model B jmp 3->2; 3 cycles either way.

original:
lda #1
        sta fe
proposal: inc fe                      ; fe was 0: bne @count fell through
cycles: 5 -> 5 on both.
assumption: fe = 0 here: 'lda fe / bne @count' fell through and inrange does not write fe. fe is zero page ($B4). A and flags dead: @ret rts returns to process_object, whose next instruction is setbank's lda (logic.s:1984).
argument: inc of 0 stores 1, as lda #1 / sta fe did. A is left 0 (from the lda vy / ora vy+1 that fell through) instead of 1; A and flags are dead at the rts.
review: fe = 0 here (lda fe/bne @count fell through; inrange does not write fe); fe is zp $B4. inc fe stores 1 and leaves N=0,Z=0 as lda #1 did; only A differs (0 vs 1), and A is dead: rts to process_object staged path whose next instruction is setbank's lda #.

original:
bitimm 3
        bne @done
proposal:
.if ::MODELB
        and #3                      ; bitimm's save and restore of A are not needed:
        bne @done                   ; A is reloaded
        lda fe
  .else
        bitimm 3
        bne @done
  .endif
cycles: Master unchanged. Model B: taken 15+3 -> 2+3; fall through 15+2 -> 2+2+3.
assumption: A = fe before (lda fe on the line above); the next instruction after the fall-through is cmp #12, which sets N, Z and C, so the flags the bitimm left are not consumed (bitimm left C from before, also unused since cmp overwrites it). @done is rts (A dead). mtmp, which bitimm wrote, is scratch owned by the expansions.
argument: On the Model B: and #3 gives Z = (fe & 3) == 0 exactly as bitimm's php/plp did; lda fe restores A = fe for the chain below. Master keeps bit #3.
review: Model B only. A = fe (lda fe). and #3 gives Z exactly as bitimm's php/plp did; V untouched in both; bne @done (rts, A dead); fall-through reloads A=fe for cmp #12, which overwrites N/Z/C. mtmp is expansion scratch (written before read by every expansion). Master keeps bit #3. Model B 10->6 bytes; taken 18->5, fall-through 17->7 cycles.

original:
cmp #12
        bcs :+
        lsr
        bra @set
:       cmp #37
        bcc @six
        lda #48
        sbc fe                      ; carry is already set: bcc fell through
        lsr
        bra @set
@six:   lda #6
proposal:
cmp #12
        bcc @half                   ; fe < 12: fe >> 1
        cmp #37
        lda #6                      ; lda keeps C from the cmp
        bcc @set
        lda #48
        sbc fe                      ; carry is already set: bcc fell through
@half:  lsr
assumption: A = fe on arrival (lda fe; bitimm/and-reload keeps it). @six has no other referrer (grep: only bcc @six); @set's other referrers are within this block.
anon_change: Removes the anonymous label at line 3066 (': cmp #37') and its only reference (bcs :+ at 3063). No other anonymous reference crosses it: the previous ':' is 3009 (ob_flame, referenced from 3004 bne :+) and there is no ':-' between 3066 and ob_switch's first anonymous label. Verified by assembling.
argument: fe<12: bcc @half -> lsr -> fe>>1 (was lsr / bra @set). 12..36: cmp #37 C=0, lda #6 keeps C, bcc @set: q1=6 (was bcc @six / lda #6). >=37: C=1, lda #48 / sbc fe / lsr falls into @set (was the same then bra @set). A at @set identical on every path; flags at @set are dead (sta q1 then mov16's lda).
review: A = fe on arrival. fe<12: bcc @half -> lsr -> fe>>1; 12..36: cmp #37 C=0, lda #6 keeps C, bcc @set -> 6; >=37: C=1, lda #48/sbc fe/lsr falls into @set. A at @set identical on every path; flags dead (sta q1, mov16, tilexy starts with lda/cmp). @six has no other reference. Removed ':' at 3066 was referenced only by 3063's bcs :+; 3004 bne :+ targets 3009, next :- is at 3205 targeting 3202. Cycles 9->7, 12->11, 19->17.

original:
@set:   sta q1
        ; tiles at (ox>>3, oy>>3) and +1 : codes from header per page
        mov16 qx, ox
        mov16 qy, oy
        jsr tilexy
        stx q4                      ; tile x (q4/q5: gx/gy are the live grid-walk cursor)
        sta q5                      ; tile y
        ldx q1
        lda LV_HDR+8,x
        sta q2
        lda LV_HDR+9,x
        sta q3
        ldx q4
        lda q5
        jsr maptile                 ; sets mapptr, Y = tx
        lda q2
        jsr mapput
        iny
        lda q3
        jsr mapput
        lda q4
        ldx q5
        jsr m_mark_dirty
        lda q4
        inca
        ldx q5
        jsr m_mark_dirty
proposal:
@set:   sta q1
        ; tiles at (ox>>3, oy>>3) and +1 : codes from header per page
        mov16 qx, ox
        mov16 qy, oy
        jsr tilexy                  ; X = tile x, A = tile y
        sta q5                      ; tile y (q4/q5: gx/gy are the live grid-walk cursor)
        jsr maptile                 ; sets mapptr, Y = tx; X kept, bank 7 back
        ldx q1
        lda LV_HDR+8,x
        jsr mapput                  ; X and Y kept
        iny
        sty q4                      ; tile x + 1
        lda LV_HDR+9,x
        jsr mapput
        dey
        tya                         ; tile x
        ldx q5
        jsr m_mark_dirty
        lda q4
        ldx q5
        jsr m_mark_dirty
cycles: Straight line; non-call instructions 45 -> 26 cycles on the Master, 54 -> 26 on the Model B (inca was 11).
assumption: (1) maptile keeps X: maptile = jsr maprow / txa / tay / jmp mapbyte (logic.s:305); Master maprow (engine.s:4533) uses A,Y only and ends jmp pagelogic; Model B maprow (engine.s:4513) saves and restores X explicitly; mapbyte and mapput (engine.s:4545,4553) touch A only; pagelogic (engine.s:4734) keeps A, X, Y and C. So X = tile x at maptile (as ldx q4 gave) and X = q1 across both mapputs, Y = tx then tx+1 across mapput. (2) The same bank is paged when LV_HDR is read: before, at handler entry (process_object has BANK_LVL in to read O_*); now, after maptile/mapput, whose pagelogic pages BANK_LVL on both targets. (3) q2, q3 and q4 are scratch: every read of them in src/ and modelb/src (logic.s 322-783 getinfo/getaltitude/object init, 3120-3147 ob_switch) is preceded by a write in the same routine, so their final values (q2 now tilexy's, q3 unchanged, q4 = tx+1 instead of tx) are never observed. q1 keeps its original final value. (4) mark_dirty clobbers Y (tay), so the tx+1 for the second call comes from memory (q4) as before, and the call order is unchanged.
argument: Original: stage LV_HDR+8/9,x into q2/q3 before maptile, reload X=q4/A=q5 for maptile, pass q2/q3 to mapput, then mark (q4, q5) and (q4+1, q5). New: tilexy's X/A go straight to maptile (A=ty still in A after sta q5); the header bytes are loaded (X=q1) straight into A for each mapput; after the iny, Y = tx+1 is kept in q4; dey/tya gives tx for the first mark_dirty and lda q4 gives tx+1 for the second (was lda q4 / inca). Map writes, their addresses and the mark_dirty arguments and order are identical. C into the second m_mark_dirty is whatever the first left, as with inca (which preserves C).
review: tilexy returns X = tx (tax) and A = ty on every exit that the original also consumed unchecked; maptile (maprow keeps X on both targets, txa/tay, mapbyte) keeps X and Y; mapput keeps X and Y; pagelogic keeps A/X/Y/C and leaves bank 7 (the bank the code executes from, so LV_HDR is read in the same bank as before). Map writes, addresses, mark_dirty arguments and order identical; C/N/Z into second m_mark_dirty identical (inca preserved C; lda q4 = tx+1). q2/q3/q4 final values differ but every reader (tilexy, getaltitude, level_init, ob_switch) writes them first; q1 and q5 unchanged. mark_dirty does not read Y. Bytes 52->39 Master, 57->39 Model B.

original: stza fe
proposal: stz fe                      ; A dead: rts to process_object's setbank
cycles: Master: stz either way. Model B: pha/lda/sta/pla 3+2+3+4=12 -> lda/sta 5.
assumption: A dead after @done rts: process_object @gen (logic.s:1983-1984) follows jsr @call with setbank BANK_LVL (lda #). Flags dead likewise (stz on the Model B leaves Z=1 where stza left Z from pla of 48; nothing reads them).
argument: stza preserves A around the store; A is not used after the rts, so stz (the A-dead spelling in cpu.inc) is equivalent.
review: @done is rts to process_object staged path (setbank's lda # next), so A and flags are dead; stza (pha/lda/sta/pla, 6 bytes) -> stz (lda/sta, 4 bytes) on Model B, identical stz on Master. 12->5 cycles on Model B.

original:
stx q4                      ; tile x (q4/q5: gx/gy are the live grid-walk cursor)
        sta q5                      ; tile y
        ldx q1
        lda LV_HDR+8,x
        sta q2
        lda LV_HDR+9,x
        sta q3
        ldx q4
        lda q5
        jsr maptile                 ; sets mapptr, Y = tx
        lda q2
        jsr mapput
        iny
        lda q3
        jsr mapput
proposal:
stx q4                      ; tile x (q4/q5: gx/gy are the live grid-walk cursor)
        sta q5                      ; tile y
        jsr maptile                 ; X = tx, A = ty (tilexy's): sets mapptr, Y = tx
        ldx q1                      ; the map calls keep X, and leave BANK_LVL selected
        lda LV_HDR+8,x
        jsr mapput
        iny
        lda LV_HDR+9,x
        jsr mapput
cycles: Straight line: 55 -> 37 cycles on both targets. Removed: the q2/q3 staging, ldx q4, lda q5, lda q2 and lda q3. The maptile/mapput bodies are unchanged.
assumption: (1) tilexy (logic.s:314) returns X = qx>>3 and A = qy>>3, exactly what lines 3078-3079 store and lines 3085-3086 reload into X/A for maptile. (2) maptile (logic.s:305) does jsr maprow / txa / tay / jmp mapbyte. maprow preserves X on both targets: on the Master (engine.s ~4532) it uses only Y; on the Model B (engine.s:4512) it saves and restores X with pha/pla. mapbyte and mapput (engine.s:4545,4553) touch only A and the bank, and both end in jmp pagelogic, which preserves A,X,Y,C (engine.s:4734). So X = q1 survives the first mapput and indexes the second LV_HDR load. (3) None of maprow/mapbyte/mapput/pagelogic writes q1; the 'q1 = page' in the comment at logic.s:301 is stale. (4) Every map call ends in pagelogic (BANK_LVL). That is the bank LV_HDR ($8000) was read in originally, so LV_HDR+8/9 read the same bytes after the calls. (5) q2/q3 are transient temps ($C4/$C5) that nothing reads afterwards: not ob_vanish (lines 3093-3104 use q4, q5, fe), not the process_object store-back (logic.s:1985-2006), and not its callers (logic.s:1059-1063, 1100-1102). (6) maptile ignores Y and C on entry: on the Master maprow starts with tay; on the Model B maprow never reads Y, and its first use of C is set by an lsr.
argument: Original: store tx,ty; X=q1; q2=HDR[8+q1]; q3=HDR[9+q1]; X=tx; A=ty; maptile; mapput(q2) at tx; iny; mapput(q3) at tx+1. New: X and A still hold tx and ty from tilexy, so maptile is called first with identical inputs. Then X=q1, which mapput preserves, feeds HDR[8+q1] and HDR[9+q1] straight to the two mapputs at Y=tx and tx+1. The map writes, q4/q5 and the exit bank are all the same. A after the second mapput equals the old q3 and is dead anyway (next is lda q4).
review: Original matches 3078-3092. X/A from tilexy are stored and reloaded unchanged, so maptile gets the same inputs. X survives maptile/mapput on both targets: Master maprow uses Y only, Model B maprow does pha/pla X, and mapbyte/mapput/pagelogic leave X alone. LV_HDR ($8000, bank 7 LGCLVL) is read after pagelogic has selected BANK_LVL. q2/q3 are scratch that is written before it is read everywhere (grep). Assembled: Master LOGIC and Model B LGCCODE shrink as claimed (34->22 bytes).

original:
lda q4
        inca
        ldx q5
proposal:
.if MODELB
        ldx q4                      ; inca is 6 bytes here
        inx
        txa
  .else
        lda q4
        inca
  .endif
        ldx q5
cycles: Master: text identical (5 bytes, 8 cy). Model B: lda q4 + inca (sta/inc/lda mtmp) is 8 bytes and 14 cy; ldx q4/inx/txa is 4 bytes and 7 cy. The ldx q5 is unchanged.
assumption: inx wraps exactly as inc mtmp does, so no assumption about q4's value is needed. Both forms preserve C: inca is documented to keep carry, and ldx/inx/txa do not touch it. X is reloaded by the following ldx q5, so its intermediate value is dead. mtmp ($DF) is scratch only (cpu.inc contract).
argument: Model B: A = q4+1 mod 256 either way and C is unchanged; N/Z are overwritten by ldx q5. The Master path is unchanged.
review: Model B: lda q4 + inca (sta/inc/lda mtmp) is 8 bytes and 14 cy; ldx q4/inx/txa is 4 bytes and 7 cy. A is the same, C is untouched, and X is dead (ldx q5 follows). The Master text is unchanged.

original:
lda fe
        cmp #48
        bne @done
        stza fe
proposal:
lda fe
        eor #48                     ; A = 0 when fe = 48 (A and C dead on return)
        bne @done
        sta fe
cycles: Master: cmp and eor are both 2 cy, and stz fe = sta fe = 3 cy, so no change. Model B: stza (pha/lda#0/sta/pla, 12 cy) becomes sta fe (3 cy). The not-equal path is identical.
assumption: ob_vanish is only reached through the jmpx table (logic.s:2037), on the staged path (type 11 >= NLEAN=2). process_object then does setbank BANK_LVL (lda #) and an lda/sta store-back before returning (logic.s:1985-2006), so A is dead. That store-back does not touch C, and C is dead at both callers: logic.s:1059 goes setbank / ldx bent / lda LV_BNEXT,x / bra @walk -> cmp #$FF; logic.s:1100 goes inc BINI / bra @rl2 -> cpx NOTHL. Z/N are overwritten the same way. The two targets already disagree on Z at this rts (Master Z=1, Model B Z=0), which fits flags being dead. fe = $B4, zero page.
argument: eor #48 sets Z exactly when fe = 48, as cmp #48 does. On the equal path A = 0, so sta fe writes 0, the same as stz fe. At rts only A and C differ: A = fe^48 instead of fe or 48, and C is not set by eor. Both are dead. @done and the earlier bne @done are unchanged.
review: eor #48 gives Z iff fe=48, and then A=0 so sta fe stores 0. A, C and N/Z are dead at return: ob_vanish is reached only via the jmpx table on the staged path, the store-back reloads A, and the callers at 1059 (setbank, ldx/lda, @walk cmp) and 1100 (inc BINI, cpx) overwrite the flags. The Model B stza (6 bytes) becomes sta zp (2 bytes).

original:
dey
        dey
        jsr mapbyte
        sta q2
        iny
        jsr mapbyte
        sta q3
        iny
        lda q2
        jsr mapput
        iny
        lda q3
        jsr mapput
proposal:
dey
        dey
        jsr mapbyte                 ; A = (row),fa-2
        iny
        iny
        jsr mapput                  ; -> (row),fa
        dey
        jsr mapbyte                 ; A = (row),fa-1
        iny
        iny
        jsr mapput                  ; -> (row),fa+1
cycles: One loop iteration: 46 -> 38 cycles on both targets, plus the unchanged mapbyte/mapput bodies.
assumption: maptile returns Y = X = fa (logic.s:305-309; maprow keeps X). mapbyte and mapput preserve Y (engine.s:4544,4552), and both end in pagelogic, which keeps A,X,Y,C. q2/q3 ($C4/$C5) are transient temps that nothing reads afterwards: the rest of the loop and @set/@draw use fa, q5, q4 and fd; the process_object store-back and its callers do not read them; m_addsprite is engine code with its own zero page. Y is dead after the second mapput: lines 3139-3148 do not read it, m_mark_dirty clobbers it, and the loop restarts at ldx fa / lda q5 / jsr maptile, which sets Y.
argument: Original: read m[fa-2] -> q2 and m[fa-1] -> q3, then write m[fa]=q2 and m[fa+1]=q3. New: read m[fa-2] and write it straight to m[fa], then read m[fa-1] and write it to m[fa+1]. The only reordering is that m[fa-1] is now read after m[fa] is written. They are different cells (fa-1 and fa in the same row, distinct mod 256), so every read sees the same value and the final map is identical. The write order (fa then fa+1) is unchanged, and Y still ends at fa+1.
review: The four cells fa-2, fa-1, fa and fa+1 are distinct mod 256, so reading fa-1 after writing fa gives the same value. At exit Y=fa+1 and A=m[fa-1], as before. q2/q3 are dead. Each mapput has its own wrsel, so interleaving it with mapbyte is safe on the write-select boards. 25->19 bytes, 22->14 cy of overhead.

original:
lda fa
        inca
        ldx q5
proposal:
.if MODELB
        ldx fa                      ; inca is 6 bytes here
        inx
        txa
  .else
        lda fa
        inca
  .endif
        ldx q5
cycles: Master: text identical. Model B: lda fa + inca is 8 bytes and 14 cy; ldx fa/inx/txa is 4 bytes and 7 cy.
assumption: Same as the ob_vanish instance: both forms preserve C, X is reloaded immediately by ldx q5, and mtmp is scratch only.
argument: Model B: A = fa+1 mod 256 and C is unchanged; the flags are overwritten by ldx q5.
review: Same as index 1: X is reloaded by ldx q5 and C is preserved. Model B saves 4 bytes and 7 cy.

original:
@set:   lda #1
        sta fd
proposal: @set:   inc fd                      ; fd = 0 here (bne @draw fell through): now 1
cycles: lda #1 (2) + sta zp (3) = 5 cy; inc zp = 5 cy. Same on both targets. A differs, but @draw reloads it.
assumption: fd ($B2, zero page) is 0 on every path to @set. ob_switch starts with lda fd / bne @draw. Between there and @set the only things that run are inrange (A,X), addscore (score, BARDIRTY), the SFXREQ store, q4/q5, the map helpers and m_mark_dirty. None of them writes fd: it is a fixed logic-owned zp address, and the original already relies on it surviving m_addsprite for the store-back. @set is reached by beq @set and by the loop fall-through; A is not used before @draw reloads it with lda fd.
argument: fd goes 0 -> 1 in both versions. At @draw, lda fd loads 1. inc sets N=0,Z=0 as lda #1 does, and lda fd overwrites them anyway.
review: fd ($B2) is 0 on both paths to @set (bne @draw fell through). inrange, addscore/bar_touch, the map helpers, m_mark_dirty and farcall never write $B2: engine ZEROPAGE ends below $A3 on both maps, and the Model B fixed zp equates are $A3-$A7 and $DF-$EF. inc zp is 5 cy, the same as lda#/sta zp.         sta lastkeys
        sta mcount                  ; last drawn frame   (menu_list's variables: this

  .repeat 16, k
        .byte (TP_CLEO0 + (($E79E79 >> (2*k)) & 3)) | ((TP_CLEO0 + 4 + ((441 >> (2*k)) & 3)) << 3)
  .endrepeat

@cbh:   .byte >CRTCB_A, >CRTCB_B

        lda tmp2
        jsr @lines

        lda tmp3
        sta SECTAB+7,x

        clc
        adc #8
        tax
        lda tmp2
        deca

        asl

        clc
        lda w16
        adc mulrowlo,y
        sta w16
        lda w16+1
        adc mulrowhi,y
        sta w16+1
@wrap:  lda w16+1
        cmp #>RINGCHARS

        bne :+

        cmp #<RINGCHARS
        bcc :++
:       lda w16
        sec
        sbc #<RINGCHARS
        sta w16
        lda w16+1
        sbc #>RINGCHARS

X at return is unchanged (the 8271 path does ldx dsk_drv; the 1770 path always reaches ldx #20 at @wrd). Y at return changes (it was rem-10), but no return path reads Y: ld_begin -> load_level_b/load_title_b, and ldprog readfile -> section (tay), bcopy (ldy) or rts. Y stays 0 through the @track retries because i_idle, i_param, wait_done, w_wait and the NMI stubs never write Y. Nothing else references @drem. This is not a sector loop or NMI handler, and the 1770 delay loop and 8271 handshakes are unchanged. Built in a scratch copy: with all four read_sectors/wait_done candidates LGCCODE goes 0x2A0A -> 0x29FA, 12 of those bytes from this one.

The fixed version keeps 11 cycles for drive 0 (lda 2, ldx 4, beq taken 3, nop 2) and 13 for drive 1 (lda 2, ldx 4, beq not taken 2, lda 2, bne taken 3). ; ---------------------------------------------------------------- the loader
; The NMI stubs go to their page and the load-time program to LDPROG, then it runs:
; it comes back with bank 7 paged and the display RAM it used as scratch.
        .import __NMISTUB_LOAD__: absolute
disc_boot:
        ldx #(nmi_end - nmi_page - 1)
:       lda __NMISTUB_LOAD__,x      ; the stubs' bytes are in this bank; their labels
        sta NMIPAGE,x               ; are their run addresses (cleo_b.cfg)
        dex
        bpl :-
        lda dsk_type
        beq :+
        lda #<NMI_W                 ; a 1770: the page's jump goes to its stub
        sta NMIPAGE+1
        lda #>NMI_W
        sta NMIPAGE+2
:       lda #<F_LDPROG_SEC
        sta ld_sec
        lda #>F_LDPROG_SEC
        sta ld_sec+1
        lda #F_LDPROG_N
        sta ld_n
        lda #<LDPROG
        sta ld_dst
        lda #>LDPROG
        sta ld_dst+1
        jmp read_sectors

; X = level index 0..15: everything the level needs into the banks (the palette is
; black; the game's load_level goes on from the header afterwards)
load_level_b:
        stx ld_level
        jsr music_stop
        jsr ld_begin
        ldx ld_level
        jsr LDPROG                  ; lv_load
        jmp ld_resume

; the menu overlay into bank 5 and the title pack into bank 6
load_title_b:
        jsr ld_begin
        jsr LDPROG+3                ; title_load
ld_resume:                          ; (interrupts still off)
        lda #LDR7                   ; the frame is the standard one: the vsync re-phase
        sta curR7                   ; keeps it so until the bar step (display.s)
        lda #$42
        sta VIA_IFR                 ; a vsync flag raised meanwhile is stale
        cli
        rts

; restarts T1 for the bar step), interrupts off, and bank 5's ldstop5 (display.s has
; the story) takes that T1 and makes the bar's frame the standard one
ld_begin:
        lda vsyncs
:       cmp vsyncs
        beq :-
        sei
        farjsr F_LDSTOP
        jmp disc_boot

        sta ROMSEL

        .import __LOWCODE_SIZE__: absolute   ; (LOAD and RUN: cpu.inc, for the bank patches)

proposal:
; A bank cannot page itself out and carry on: the instruction after the switch is
; read from the new bank.  So each switch lands on its continuation: entry's, at
; $8040 in bank 7, on start6 at $8047 in bank 6; bank 6's to7, the same seven bytes
; at $8040 there, on the jmp start7 at $8047 in bank 7.
entry:  bankimm lda, BANK_MAP, BANK_LVL
        sta ROMSEL_CPY
        sta ROMSEL                  ; the next fetch is bank 6's start6
        .assert * = BANKCODE + 7, error, "entry's switch must end where start6 begins"
        jmp start7                  ; bank 6's to7 lands here, in bank 7

        .segment "MAPLO"            ; bank 6
        .import __LOWCODE_SIZE__: absolute   ; (LOAD and RUN: cpu.inc, for the bank patches)
to7:    bankimm lda, BANK_LVL, BANK_MAP ; start6's way out: the next fetch is bank 7's
        sta ROMSEL_CPY              ; jmp start7, at the same address
        sta ROMSEL
start6:
        .assert * = BANKCODE + 7, error, "start6 must follow entry's switch"
        sei
        ldx #$3F                    ; the stack is 64 bytes: $0100-$013F
        txs

The 6502 fetches the opcode after `sta ROMSEL` from the NEW bank (the file's own comment, lines 10-11, states it; it is why the old code ran from RAM). @dir:   lda PB_MAP                  ; the directory's bank, for both paths
        jsr pgbank
        ldy #0
        lda (lp),y
        sta item
        cmp #$FF
        beq @dnone
        jsr findplace               ; src -> the placement entry, or C set
        bcs @dnone

        ldy #3
        lda (src),y

        ldy #1
        lda (src),y                 ; the bank: bank 6's images carry the flag
        cmp #BANK_MAP
        bne :+
        ldy #6
        lda (lp),y
        ora #$10
        sta (dst),y
:       ldy #4                      ; the mask: X = lo, Y = hi
        lda (src),y
        tax
        iny
        lda (src),y
        tay
@dmask: lda PB_LVL
        jsr pgbank              ; box ids (the last 15) have no entry
        lda nt
        cmp #16
        bcc @dnext
        tya
        ldy #1
        sta (ent),y
        txa
        dey
        sta (ent),y
        bcs @dnext                  ; (C set: the cmp)
@dnone: lda #0
        ldy #7
:       sta (dst),y
        dey
        bpl :-
        tax                         ; no mask: X = Y = 0
        tay
        beq @dmask
@dnext:
cycles: Model B only. P = jsr pgbank incl. rts (~64 cy). Found path, nt<16: old 4+P+3+2+3 +4+P after the flag test = 16+2P; new 18 (ldy/lda/tax/iny/lda/tay) +4+P+3+2+3 = 30+P. Found, nt>=16: old 48+2P, new 52+P. None path (item $FF or findplace C set): old dnone pgbank(PB_MAP) moved before the item test (same count), then +7 (tax/tay/beq) and +5 for nt>=16 (tya..bcs vs lda#0..sta), minus the dropped @dnext pgbank (4+P). ldy #2 -> iny: 2->2. Every path faster by >= P-12; not timing-critical (load-time, display black).
assumption: (1) The PB_MAP page is only needed for the (dst) stores: everything the @dir loop reads before them is main RAM -- lp=sprdir inside ldprog ($0E00..), item/src/zp, findplace->section reads STAGE_LVL=$5C00 and the placement list there (ldprog.s:605-615, 672-688); pgbank keeps X and Y (ldprog.s:139-151). (2) The PB_LVL page at @dnext was redundant: every path into @dnext already did lda PB_LVL/jsr pgbank (lines 527-528 or 548-549) and nothing between pages anything else (the (ent) stores are to SPRMASK=$BF14 in bank 7, which is why the earlier pgbank(PB_LVL) must stay). (3) X is dead in the loop and after it: nothing in 496-580 reads X, and after the loop section (uses Y) is followed by ldx PB_TILES (line 593). Y is reloaded by ldy #0 at @dir. (4) pgbank returns A=PB_LVL, keeps X, Y (wrx touches only A); C after cmp #16 not taken is 1 and tya/ldy/sta/txa/dey/sta leave C alone, so bcs @dnext is always taken.
anon_change: none: the three ':' lines (copy loop, after the flag store, the dnone clear loop) are all kept and nothing new is added; bne :-, bne :+, bpl :- keep their targets
argument: Hoist: lda PB_MAP/jsr pgbank moved from the found path (after findplace) and from @dnone to @dir, so both paths still page bank 6 exactly once before their (dst) stores. ldy #2 after ldy #1/sta -> iny (Y 1->2, same N/Z). Mask: found path loads X=src[4], Y=src[5] (main RAM, any bank), falls into @dmask = the old pgbank(PB_LVL)/nt test; if nt>=16: tya/ldy #1/sta (ent),y writes ent[1]=src[5], txa/dey/sta writes ent[0]=src[4] (old: ent[0]=src[4], ent[1]=src[5]), then bcs @dnext (C=1). @dnone: clears dst[0..7] as before (A=0 at loop exit, Y=$FF), tax/tay make X=Y=0 with Z=1, beq @dmask -> pgbank(PB_LVL), nt test, writes 0,0 to ent[1],ent[0] (old: 0,0). The @dnext pgbank(PB_LVL) is dropped (redundant, see assumption 2); the loop still exits with bank 7 paged since every path passes @dmask. Assembled in a scratch copy: $371..$3F9 (136 bytes) -> $370..$3DC (108).
review: Original matches 496..559. Hoisted pgbank(PB_MAP) is safe: everything read before the (dst) stores is main RAM (lp=sprdir in LDPROG at $0E00, item zp, section/findplace read STAGE_LVL=$5C00); C at bcs comes from findplace. iny for ldy #2 (Y=1). Anonymous ':' count unchanged (3), bne :+ now lands on ldy #4. @dmask is a new cheap label, no clash. Every path saves ~P-18 cy or more (P~65). Load-time code, not timing-critical. Assembled: -28 bytes.

assumption: (1) <STAGE = <MENU_BASE = <TITLE_ADDR = 0 (build/defs_ld.inc: STAGE=$1C00, MENU_BASE=TILES=$8100, TITLE_ADDR=$8900 from assets.inc / convert.py 0x8900). The .assert enforces this at build time. (2) stage (ldprog.s:623) sets dst=STAGE, so dst lo = 0 after it. readfile (ldprog.s:84) writes only tmp in zp. read_sectors (disc.s:94) and its helpers i_idle/i_param/wait_done/w_wait write no zero page (only ld_* in LGCBSS, NMI-page cells and FDC registers). The NMI stubs (disc.s:26-80) write only self-modified absolute addresses and NMI-page cells. The disc data goes to STAGE ($1C00+, at most 46 sectors, so below $4A00), not zp. IRQs are off (ld_begin, disc.s:316 sei), so no IRQ handler touches $A8-$AD. (3) bcopy (ldprog.s:109) changes only src+1 and dst+1 in zp (the incs in @page). It only reads src lo, dst lo, cnt and cnt+1. wrx and pgbank touch no zp. So after the first bcopy and the second stage, src lo = 0, cnt lo = 0 and dst lo = 0 still hold. src+1 and dst+1 (moved on by bcopy, or set to >STAGE by stage) are written again. (4) There is no label inside title_load. Its only entry is jmp title_load at ldprog.s:46, so nothing enters it partway.

The hi bytes are unchanged. Block 2: src lo and cnt lo still hold 0 from block 1 because nothing writes them in between. dst lo = 0 from stage, which equals <TITLE_ADDR. src+1, dst+1 and cnt+1 are loaded again as before. A at bcopy entry is different, but bcopy overwrites A in wrx before any use. X is set by ldx as before. Flags at bcopy entry are dead: bcopy starts with stx/stx/jsr wrx, and wrx does an lda.
review: Original matches lines 738-770 exactly. STAGE=$1C00, MENU_BASE=TILES=$8100 and TITLE_ADDR=$8900 (modelb/build/defs_ld.inc) are all page-aligned, and the added .assert enforces that. stage sets dst=STAGE (lo 0) with X. readfile writes only tmp ($AE) in zero page. read_sectors, i_idle, i_param, wait_done and w_wait write only LGCBSS, NMI-page cells and FDC registers. The NMI stubs write through self-modified absolute addresses into STAGE. IRQs are off (sei in ld_begin). bcopy writes only src+1 and dst+1 (and ROMSEL_CPY $F4). wrx and pgbank write no zero page in $A8-$AD. So src lo, cnt lo and dst lo are still 0 at the second bcopy. A and flags at bcopy entry are dead (stx/stx/jsr wrx, and wrx starts with lda). The only entry is jmp title_load at line 46, and no label sits inside. Bytes: 70 -> 52, 18 saved. Every path is faster. original:

        tax

        sta (zdst),y
        lda #>WRSEL_WATFORD

        sta (zdst),y
        lda #>WRSEL_SOLIDISK

        sta (zdst),y
@wnext: lda zsrc
        clc
        adc #4
        sta zsrc
        bcc @wfix
        inc zsrc+1
        jmp @wfix

; Which sockets hold RAM, and which four the game gets.  The test is the one Stuart
; McConnachie's sideways RAM Elite loader used (1988; Mark Moxon's commentary): page
; the bank through $F4 and ROMSEL, flip bit 0 of the ROM type byte at $8006 and see
; whether it stuck, put it back.  A floating bus fails it (both reads see the same
; value), a write-protected board fails it too -- it looks like ROM, and the message
; says so.  First the board: the test is run over the 16 banks writing through ROMSEL
; alone, then again selecting the write bank the Watford way ($FF30 + bank), then the
; Solidisk way (user VIA port B, bits 0-3 made outputs); the board is the way that
; finds the MOST banks (a board's write latch rests on some bank, usually 0, so the
; plain test "finds" that one bank on a board machine too), plain winning a tie; and
; every write below goes through wrx.  A machine with RAM of two kinds gets the kind
; with more.  Every bank then gets a class: 0, RAM with no ROM image in it; 1, RAM with
; an image the MOS is not running (no entry in its table at $02A1: left there by an
; earlier load); 2, RAM holding a ROM the MOS recognised -- taken only when nothing
; else is left, which is safe here because nothing calls the MOS once the pieces go
; down.  Two socket numbers that reach the same RAM (a board answering two numbers)
; are found by a signature written to each and read back -- not Elite's byte-for-byte
; comparison of the banks, which would call four blank banks one -- and the extra
; numbers dropped.  The four are the lowest-numbered of the best class.

        sta board
        jsr @count

        sta bestb
        lda #BOARD_WATFORD

        beq :+
        sta best
        lda #BOARD_WATFORD
        sta bestb

        sta $FE62
        lda #BOARD_SOLIDISK
        sta board
        jsr @count
        cmp best
        bcc :+
        beq :+
        sta best
        lda #BOARD_SOLIDISK
        sta bestb
:       lda bestb
        sta board
        cmp #BOARD_SOLIDISK         ; not a Solidisk: give the user port back
        beq @classify
        lda #0
        sta $FE62

@b:     stx ROMSELC

@bsc:   sta score,x
@bnext: dex

@sig:   lda score,x

        jsr wrx

        txa
